Intended writing last Friday but kept putting it off. We certainly had a great Thanksgiving dinner. I’ll mail you the menu. It’s too large to enclose. Hope you all enjoyed Thanksgiving as well as I did as far as the dinner was concerned. I’d rather have been home though. Sure was tickled to get Knox’s letter. He does’t seem to think much of Papa’s hunting abilities. Said Papa had gone hunting and got nothing as usual. Ha. Lordy I’d like to be there and go hunting.
Say I haven’t got a pair of skates around there have I? The river is Frozen and I’d like to go skating. Can’t buy any this pay day account not getting any pay until January. Didn’t get to sign the pay role for some reason or other. Never mind about them though if there isn’t a pair there. I’ll manage to borrow some skates from some one.
I received the Pike County Republic other day. Get it regularly. Noticed my name in it as one of the boys from Pike in service.
Wonder who is sending me that paper?
Got a dandy letter from Les Wildt other day. Have been corresponding with him ever since you gave me his address.
I get a sweater, 2 pair socks and a helmet from the Red Cross today. Sure are nice but the sweater isn’t as good as the one I got from home. I can use them both cause its awful cold out riding each morning. My hands and feet nearly freeze when out riding. I’m going to mail my summer clothes home. Can’t take them to France. I’ve 3 or 4 pair Khaki trousers that would make Knox good hunting clothes to wear over others. Also 4 or 5 suits summer underwear. Haven’t room to take care of them. If I’m still in the army next summer I’ll get more. Got a baseball sweater that Knox might use too.
Do you remember me telling you some time ago about getting a card from Alabama N.Y. and no signature on it? I just ran across the card today and will enclose it. Perhaps you can figure who sent it. Looks like Tom Blair’s writing. Was he in Albany month or so ago?
We had moving pictures here (YMCA) last night of our company out on wire drill. They were good and plain. I wasn’t in it. Was in another section 5 miles out when the pictures were being taken.
Glad the girls got their passes ok. Will write them at Morrisonville. Golly I’d give anything to be home Christmas but no chance. Aside from being unable to get a furlough it would take about $50.00 to make the trip. Besides I don’t know whether or not we’ll be here Christmas. I saw a stencil in orderly room other day marked “Co B 17BSC” port of Embarkation Hoboken, NY but can’t tell a great deal about that. Think they just have the stamp on hand ready in case we do go right away.
Well they are putting the lights out to run some movies so must stop. Intended to write more tonight but no light. Everybody write often.
Lots Love,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Little Silver, New Jersey on November 16, 1917

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike County

Little Silver, NJ
Nov 16th
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received 2 letters from Papa since last writing and mighty glad to get them. Papa sure does write regularly. I’m feeling better today although still have a bad cold. Received the sweater from Bess today. Gee – It’s a dandy letter. Just what I wanted. Came in mighty handy today. T’was awful cold and we were out on a full pack inspection.
Yes Papa we have telegraphing each pm on buzzer. We don’t use anything but continental code. Guess I’ll be pretty rusty on Morse when I come out. I’ll sure be glad when this war is over. I’m getting kinda homesick. Lordy but I’d sure love to spend Christmas at Pearl.
I don’t practice visual signaling any more nearly all of the company are qualified so don’t have to practice. We have wire drill nearly every day. Also giving as instructions in ciphering. We all have a cipher disc. I don’t think we will go over before spring but of course can’t tell.
Was on guard Thursday night. Golly it was cold. Do guard duty about every 12 days. Doesn’t take long for guard to roll around. Time sure is passing quick for me. Can’t realize that I’ve been in the army 6 months.
2 of the sergeants in our company received commission as first Lieutenants today. Don’t know where they will go. Wish they were going to stay with out company. I like them both awfully well.
We have all of our winter clothing now. Good warm clothing. Hows Lucerne coming on the piano?
Was over to YMCA last night. Had Vaudeville and lunch afterwards. Some people by name of Ruinson pay for all this. Have an entertainment and something to eat every Thursday night. Sure is nice of them. All the people through this country are very hospitable. Well can’t think of much to write tonight so will close.
Glad to hear you re all well. I’m feeling good expect for cold.
Will write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Margaret Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Margaret Chandler
Mailed From: Little Silver, New Jersey on November 2, 1917

Miss Margaret Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike County

Nov 2nd, 1917
Dearest Margaret,
Received your letter some time ago and sure glad to get it. Wish you’d write often. Hows school coming? Guess you’re having a great time playing basket ball. Gee it will soon be Christmas. Seems an age since I’ve spent an Xmas at home. Sure hope I’ll be at home some Christmas. Don’t know where I’ll be this Christmas. Kinda looks as thought we were going to leave before soon. But can’t tell much about it. Didn’t expect to be here now.
Sure is cold here. Having lots rain too. Makes it awful disagreeable. I’m sure having a peach of a time in the kitchen. Lots of work to do. Get up at 5:30 am and work until 6:30 pm. Wash dishes, pans, peel spuds, onions, and do a little bit of everything. Carry coal and cut wood each day. I’ll be off tomorrow night and I’ll sure be glad of it.
Wrote Bess last night and put a 2 cent stamp on it so guess she will have to pay a penny to get it out. Didn’t think about having to put 3 cent on it.
When are you going to Morrisonville? How is Audrey? Golly Id sure love to see her and the rest of you all.
Well I don’t know anything to write tonight so will stop.
Be sure and write as often as you can cause I sure love to get the letters.
Hope everybody is well.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Santa Margarita, CA on October 25, 1917

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois
Pike County

Santa Margarita 10/25
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received 3 letters from papa in last three days and sure glad to get them. Glad to know Hulsingler wasn’t looking for me but was sure he didn’t have anything on me. I’ll probably be here for two weeks or so longer. Getting along OK. It’s getting pretty cool out here. Had 2 or 3 frosts but we never have any snow. I’ve been busy every evening rehearsing of an entertainment to be given by the Christian Endeavor a week from Friday. I’m to be the bridegroom in a mock wedding ceremony. Going to have it in the school house. They’re having lots of music and songs too. Got a good orchestra to play for them. They’re trying to raise enough money to build a new church. I went to Sell’s first circus other day in San Luis abispo. Got 4 comps for putting up posters in the depot. Gave 3 of them to the agent and wife, agent has card party every once in while and invites bunch to his house. Generally serve coffee, sandwiches, and cake. He is helping the CE entertainment also. Got 2 songs to sing – He is a swell singer- One of them is “Under the Sheltering Palms” and the other “Never Let the Same Bee Sting you Twice.” If they have any account of it in San Luis paper will send you the clipping.
Ralph is getting quite a stay at Rush Hill isn’t he? Wonder why they don’t put Micky to work.
Guess I’ll write Bess a letter tonight but I wrote her last. Business isn’t very heavy here now. Never have over 4 or 5 trains during the night. Had a derailment close to here other night and 3 passenger trains had to stay here all night until they got the track cleared. Well must stop now.
Will write more often after this.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Chandler Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Chandler Family
Stationary Info: Signal Corps Recreation House (National Leauge for Women’s Service) P.O. Little Silver N.J. Tel. 291 Red Bank

October 20th, 1917
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all,
Received Papa’s letter yesterday and sure glad to get it. Been on guard last 24 hours. Rained all night and most of the morning but, of course, that doesn’t stop one from walking post. I didn’t have my raincoat with me and I was soaked clear through. Awful cold too. The Radio Detachment left today for France. Again, some rumors that we will leave shortly but you can’t feel a thing about it. May go at any time and again may not go at all. We wear two identification tags now. Each one has our name, rank and organization on it. One to be buried with us in case of death and the other one sent to parents. So if you ever get a little round tag with my name on it you can hang out the black ribbon. I’m not worried about not coming back. Think will make it OK in case we should be sent over. Suppose you read of the American Trouspers being torpedoed by German submarine. Fortunately it was returning and not many aboard to lose though and that’s bad enough.
We are having a field meet in this camp next Wednesday. All sorts of contests. I haven’t entered in any of them. Don’t think I could compete very strong in any of the athletic events. We’re having a wire contest though, between different Battalions to see who can set up radio station and open telegraph stations in shortest length of time. Of course I’ll take part in that. Awful glad Knox’s arm is mending rapidly. Hate to see him miss so much school.
A fellow in our company received a letter from one of the boys in France today. Was dated “France, September 15th” and had been censored. Didn’t say a thing about their locations or of the conditions existing over there. Was over a month on the road so If I get over there and you don’t hear from me very often, you’ll know the reason why.
Yes it’s only four more days until papa’s birthday. Wish I had something to send him. Sure hope the men on Ca get a raise. Prices keep going up but not so the wages. Lordy I’d like to be back at work. Sure work in the Army. Fatigue nearly all the time when we’re not drilling and drilling isn’t any play. First thing after Breakfast we police up the camp. Pick up all the matches, cigarette butts, pieces of paper, etc. First call for Reville (Rev-a-le) at 5:45 am. Assembly 6 am, water and feed horses immediately after reville. Breakfast at 6:30 am then clean up camp, as I mentioned above. After get camp cleaned up we groom the horses up to 7:45 am, Calisthenics 7:45 to 8:30 am, mounted drill 8:30 am to 11 am, groom horses on return tom drill then water, feed and put on horse blankets. 1 pm to 2 pm we have visual signaling, 2 pm to 3 pm Buzzer practice. From 3 to 4 pm have nothing to do. 4 pm water and feed horses, 5 pm stand retreat and then we’re all through for the day. Friday evenings we clean equipment instead of drilling. Saturday morning is inspection and Saturday evening and all day Sunday have nothing to do except grokm and feed horses. Mounted drill on Monday is tactical, tha is =, opening telegraph stations and stringing wire cross country. The company is divided up into 4 sections, each section consisting of about 14 men, sometimes not that many. Each section taken wire cart and reel out wire across country, each connecting with one of the other sections so as to establish a complete line of communication between all sections. Each section opens two stations. The first station relating all messages to next section and so on until message has reached destination. Each section forms groups of four numbering 1 to 4 from left to right. No 1 is operator, no 2 and 4 Linemen, and No 3 the horse holder. When command is given to open station the first set of four rides around to reel at cart, reel cart being in rear of each section. All dismount dn turn their horses over to Horse Holder (No.3). The operator gets a Buzzer, ground rod, pencil and pad out of reel carts and connects onto wire, thus opening first station. The reel cart then drives on feeling out wire as it goes. The do it in a gallop. The men who didn’t take part in opening first station ride ahead of the feel cart in the formation I mentioned before and the two linemen follow the cart and see that the cart and see the wire is put in proper shape and no breaks. They patrol the line continually between stations bring responsible for its maintenance and if they find it broken at any point or someone has cut it they immediately replace it. Sometimes the Captain will cut it to see if the linemen are on the job. After we get through sending messages ect., command is given to close station. Then ge outs his instrument and other articles back in. Cart and the reel cart winds up on reel. Two men ride behind with pike poles (pool with hook on end so wire will slip through it) and see that it doesn’t get tangled up. Doesn’t take very long to string out 5 or 10 mile of wire. All sections assemble and come back into camp.
On Tuesdays and Thursday we have equilation. Think I mentioned that before. Riding without feet in stirrups, etc. Anyway I dread it most of all. It’s purpose is to train us to balnce ourselves in saddle. Wednesday and Fridays we have company drill, close order. Each section is formed in sets of fours same as in other drill except it doesn’t make any difference how we are placed or whether we’re number 1, 2, 3, or 4. This drill is just to teach us different formations such as “right, or left, about,” “right or left front into line,” “right on left flank,” so that Commander on Battle field can get his company into whatever formation he sees fit by giving the command.
well it’s getting pretty late so I’ll close and go to camp. Can’t describe very well, just what we do but its not a bit complicated.
Hope this finds every body well. I’m feeling fine, physically. Guess the fatigue we get is good for us.
Everybody write soon and Happy Birthday to papa,
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Camp Alfred Vail, Litte Silver, New Jersey on October 8, 1917

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike County

M.W. Chandler
Co B 1st FBSC
Little Silver, NJ

Camp Alfred Vail
Little Silver, NJ 9th 1917
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received 3 letters from papa since last writing and mighty glad to get them. Was so sorry to hear Knox has broken his arm and I’ll be anxious to hear when he is OK again. That will keep him out of school too. Be sure and let me know how he gets along. Nothing much new to write except were all afraid we wont get to go to France for awhile. We’re all prepared to leave but nobody know anything about when we are going. Some think the company will be split up and sent to different places as non commissioned officers to drill the National army. Everybody thought we would leave immediately and its sure some disappointment to think we might not go. Can’t tell anything about it though.
I’m on guard duty now. On at 5:30 pm yesterday and off at 5:30 this pm. Do guard duty 2 hours off four hours. It’s pretty cold here at nights but have good warm clothing and a dandy overcoat. I’ll sure be glad to get that sweater. Overcoats are so unhandy to go out to drill but got to wear something to keep warm and that sweater will make it fine and dandy.
I just got away from the guard house for few mins to come over to YMCA and write. Hands are so cold can hardly write.
I’ll be over at club tomorrow night and will write from there.
Be sure and let me know how Knox makes it. Hope rest of you are all well.
In case we leave unexpectedly will write you if permitted.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Little Silver, New Jersey on September 28, 1917

M.W. Chandler
Co “B” 1st Field Battalion
Camp Alfred Vail
Little Silver, N.J.

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill.
Pike County

Camp Alfred, Vail 26th
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Golly Havent received any mail since being here. Thought sure would have received a letter before now. Everything going along OK. Awful chilly here but otherwise like it OK. Haven’t heard anything definite as to when we will go to France but were sure going. I’m anxious to get over there. 25 Signal Corps men and 3 officers left today for Franc. 2 come over to the Signal Corps Club nearly every night. Good way to pass time away. Have a dandy Victrola and piano. All kinds books and magazines to read. Been doing lot of fatigue since coming here getting camp straightened out. I haven’t been on a horse since leaving Texas but will go out tomorrow on drill. How are the children coming in school? Is the apple season over yet papa? How much does Grace’s baby weigh now? Lordy I’d love to see her. Did she enter the contest at the state fair? Well guess I’ll go down and finish my story. Am reading “The Dark Star” by Chambers. Have to be back in camp by 11 pm. We all drew overcoats yesterday. The sure are dandy. Will get rest of our winter clothing right away. Fitzjarrellz is over here with me tonight. You know he is the fellow I mentioned from White Hall. Does Ruby remember him? He used to go with Lucille Knox.
Well must stop. Hurry up and write.
Love to all,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Fort Bliss, Texas on August 27, 1917

M.W. Chandler
Co “B” 1st F.B.S.C.
Ft. Bliss

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois
Pike County

Co “B” 1st FBSC
Ft. Bliss Texas
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received 2 letters from papa since returning from hike last Saturday evening and sure glad to get them. We went up into New Mexico on the hike. Had a dandy time. The company was split up and strung out through the country and we had continuos wire communication which we put up ourselves. I stayed on duty until midnight. A and C company were along too. A company is the Radio outfit. They put up their wireless apparatus and were in communication with El Paso all the time. They also had a wire strung to our camp and out company relayed all messages for El Paso to the Radio Co and they sent them by wireless to El Paso and Ft. Bliss.
The man who brought Papa’s letter to me yesterday saw that it was from Pearl and asked me if I knew anyone there. I told him I lived there and he said he was from White Hall. He sleeps in tent next to mine. He is a step brother of Pearl Ellis and said he remembered Ruby and Pearl were at their house one time. His name is Fitzjarrellz. He is Corporal in the company and a nice fellow. He also knows Uncle Will’s family at Manchester and used to go with Lucille. Sure surprised me to meet him. Said he had been at Pearl lots of times playing ball and coming to boat shows and knows lots of the fellows around Pearl. He’s the only fellow I’ve ran across close from home. Our battalion played baseball with 2nd telegraph battalion yesterday and beat them 7 to 3. Captain was sure pleased. I had m picture taken in ball suit with another fellow. Just a Kodak. Will send you one soon as they are finished. Mama did you ever find the Kodaks in my suit case?
Well its just 5 min until drill time and I’ve been writing this in an awful hurry so could get it off this am.
Hope everybody is OK. Well write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Fort Bliss, Texas on July 11, 1917

M.W. Chandler
Causal Camp
Ft. Bliss, Texas

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill

Casual Camp No. 2
Ft. Bliss, TX 7-11
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
No mail since last writing. Expect to be assigned some time this week. I never have received any mail forwarded from Sanderson yet. Should have a good bunch of it pretty soon. Did you get my cards from Juane & Max? Supposed you got my pictures I sent from Sanderson. I’m still doing messenger duty over at Captain’s office. Don’t have much to do. My you ought to see the soldiers drilling here. They get about 3000 out on parade ground and it sure is pretty to see them all moving. They have 6 or 8 bands playing all the time. There’s about 5 camps here at Ft. Bliss. Wouldn’t be surprised if I was assigned to one of them. Quite a bunch of infantry have been sent out of here lately. Some to Eagle Pass, TX, some to Salt Lake City, Utah and some to Syracuse. Wish they would ship me to Illinois. Lordy wish I had come home before enlisting but they told me Tuesday (Day 2 enlisted) that Saturday was last day could volunteer so I thought I’d better get in.
I’ll send my clothes home first time I go to Taylor. Got 2 suit cases full.
Sure hot down here. These uniforms are pretty warm too. Generally go to bed about 8 or 9 pm. Have breakfast at 6 am. Then after breakfast everybody helps clean up camp except men detailed for special duty. They have to pick up every match and scrap on ground and then sweep the entire camp. Some of them have to wait on tables and some work in kitchens about 5 each. I’ve worked both of them. Say I worked in kitchen. I peeled 4 bushel potatoes; scrubbed tables and washed pots. I’ve worked every job they’ve got here expect to clean toilets. We have a dandy shower bath here. Each of us received a Toilet kit yesterday free of charge. Consisting of towel, shaving soap, brush, razor, shoe brush, clothes brush, tooth brush and box shoes polish and a bag to keep them in. Also got package needles and some thread. We’re allowed about 40.00 worth clothes when we enlist. My outfit ran about 15.00. Got 3 suits summer underwear, 3 pair socks, 1 shirt and 1 uniform and pair shoes. Oh yes, got a pair overalls and jacket too. Each of us have our own mess kit consisting of fork, knife, spoon (large), and one pan. We take pan in kitchen and they fill it up. Always have radishes, onions, bread, butter, and ice tea, lemonade, or coffee on table. I’ve never got up from table hungry. We wash our own mess kit and bring them in and put them away. Have a free moving picture show over a 8th calvary every night. We’re free to go where we please from 5>45 pm to 11 pm except Sundays and holidays. We’re off all day except men detailed for special duty, as I am. I did quite a letter writing today. Took bunch papers to Camp Stewart 10 miles distant and then made several other trips on horseback and I’m pretty tired and dusty so I’ll quit and go take bath.
Expect to get a letter from Papa tomorrow for sure.
Sure hope everybody is OK.
Love to all,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed On: July 31, 1917

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ills
Pike Co

July 31st
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received letter from papa day before yesterday and one today and mighty glad to get them. General Representative of Russia was here today reviewing our troops. They had a big parade, about 12000 soldiers. Gee it sure looked pretty. As far back as I could see was column after column of soldiers. The signal corps was up toward the front, mounted. I had a pretty good house. By golly from the way paper reads the general had better beat it to Russia. Haven’t heard anything about how long will be here but couldn’t be surprised if didn’t stay here until next spring. It’s pretty warm here in day time but the night are always cool and have to cover up. Thane good thing. Awful glad the girls got their pass to Dunlap. I’ll write to them tonight in this company from Illinois. Sure seems good to see dome one from up there. What is Ralph doing? Hope he gets a job OK. I saw in paper where all the switches around Chad were on a strike. Hope it doesn’t delay the girls trip any.
Well I’m in a hurry. Got to get ready to stand retreat. Will write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Margaret Chandler, To: Ruby Chandler
item.description:
From: Margaret Chandler, To: Ruby Chandler
Mailed From: Pearl, Ill on June 9, 1917

Pearl, Ill
June, 9, 1917
Dear Ones:-
I’m having such a good time I can’t hardly find time to write. I went to Witt and driving yesterday in the car. Grace, Lorin, and Baby also went about 50 miles it was a fine ride. Ruby I do wish you could see this sweet baby. I know but I can’t express my thoughts in words. maybe Bess can tell you about her. Has Mamma come him yet? Loin and Grace have a new $200 talking machine. It is a beauty. He will have a new piano up here before long. Ruby I bet you were lonesome without anybody to go with, but Bess will soon be home.
Ruby I like my hat just fine now, but it was almost too large at first until I got the lining put in. I am going to write to Mamma & Freda first as soon as I get through here. I bet Freda is kind of lonesome, has she been down since I’ve been gone.
I am going to Sunday School tomorrow, it will be children’s day.
Loren, Bess, Lucerne, and I had our pictures taken with the baby. Loren got them today they are awful good of all of us. Grace said they were the best Kodak pictures they had eve taken of the baby.
This is all I can think of now.
Lots of love,
Margaret
If you get any letters from Mamma send them on.
M

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Sanderson on June 14, 1917

Sanderson June 13-17
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received 2 letters from papa today and sure glad to get them. Guess it’s been quite a while since I’ve written. Been feeling pretty glum lately but OK now. It’s blooming hot can’t do anything. I’m sending my resignation in tomorrow and am going to work for Western Union. May come home. I’d like to get away from this hot country, nothing but barren hills. Had big sand storm today but I was in bed and didn’t bother me any. Had my ears full of sand when I got up. Am sending you picture under separate cover. But you were all glad to see Bess, wish I could see you all. Suppose Mama will be home in a few days. Will mail three pictures. Wish you’d give Grace one. Started to mail one to Morrisonville but wasn’t sure she was there. Guess Lucerne will have a good time in Granite. Whats Knox doing anyway? Guess he is doing lots of swimming. I haven’t been swimming since left California.
Well don’t know any news. Everything quiet down here. Wont leave here for week or so yet.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Sanderson on May 31, 1917

Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
I received three letters from papa and one from mama,enclosing Lorin’s and was sure tickled to get them. First mail I had received since leaving Valentine. Sure was too bad about that cyclone. Hope no more of them come along through here. Glad that one didnt hit Pearl. From looks of things I’m going to be here for couple months unless they send a man to relieve me and let me come to El Paso. I got all the clippings Papa sent. Wouldn’t mind being with Pershings expedition if could get a good job. I went over to court house this PM and registered before County Clerk and Mailed it to registrar Pearl, care Sheriff Pittsfield. That way clerk said to address it. I enclosed stamped envelope so he could mail me a receipt. I must be there by the 5th. Should reach there in plenty of time. Golly its sure hot down here. Temperature of 110. Wish I was home. I couldn’t quit very well now if I wanted to account them being so short of operators and couldn’t get relief. This is a very large place. Like it better than Valentine though. It pays 7.50 more on the month. Is Aunt Sarah feeling OK? Hope so. She always was so good to me. Suppose Knox has stumped his toes a dozen times or so. Does he wash his feet before he goes to bed? Hope Lorin gets the job he mentioned. Gee wish I could see that kid of Grace’s. I’ll bet she is some baby. Have any of you been fishing this season yet? I’d like to be there and go squirrel hunting with Papa this season. Golly wish I was home. I only have one dispatcher to work with here. Get along fine with him. I saw him at Del Rio while back. Seems to be a nice man. Sure are a good bunch dispatchers and chiefs at El Paso. They all treat me good there and would show me about different wires and how to adjust a quad.
I worked on a quad most of time I was there. I’d be sending to Houston and Houston would be sending to Opr on other side of me all at same time on same wire. Kinda funny how it works but it does. Four men can work on the same wire, two sending and two receiving. Sure had lots messages. Run about 700 with Houston each day but I didn’t have to do very much. Just about 4 hours steady work with Houston and two hours with Los Angeles and San Francisco.
Well don’t know anything more to write. Sure glad to get that bunch of letters today. Mama hope you write again pretty soon. Papa averages a letter nearly every day and by golly they sure look good.
Hope everybody is well. Hope Vinnie gets well OK.
Love to all,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Langtry, Texas on May 9, 1917

Langtry, Tex 5/9th 1917
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Got her evening of 7th. This sure is some town. One store and 2 or 3 restaurants. Not a very heavy job. Pays $87.50 and commissions all told ought to make it pay 100 but I’ll only be here two or three days longer at least. I can stand on platform and throw across the Rio Grande into Old Mexico. Only about a hundred yards to River. Saw a whole bunch of Mexicans over there yesterday. Don’t know what they were doing. I telegraph from 9 am to 3 pm. Express Commission ran $8.00 last month. Ha. He said it was a very poor month. Don’t have very much to do. Have oil tanks here and have to contend with that but its nothing like Valentine. I kinda wish he hadn’t out me on Valentine agency cause now I’ll have to be running around working relief agencies and can’t stay on my regular job and its more expensive to be running around here and there.
Do hope Margaret is well. Awful glad to hear Lucerne made her grades. How did Knox make it? Too bad Margaret couldn’t take examination. Did I mention receiving Papas and Mamas letters enclosing Bess’? Anyway I did and mighty glad to get them. Haven’t heard anything from Cra yet but expect to in few days. Don’t suppose I could get a pass up there anyway. I got a letter from MK 2 and they said they would be glad to furnish me pass San Antonio to St. Louis provided it was ok with me that they notify this road they had issued such transportation as required by I.C.C. Upon inquiry I found out that if I get pass from MK 2 that the RHASA will blacklist me from their road. They don’t allow their employees to write for their own passes without taking up with them so that knocks me out of pass cause I don’t want to have a bad record here. I don’t see why in the dickens they should care who I get pass from. Guess if they wont furnish transportation I’ll ride the cabooses. Wouldn’t take me very long to get there. Sure will be glad when this war is over.
I’m going to work in Western Union this summer sure. It’s good for $125.00 anytime. They have established an 8 hour day and overtime on Sundays now. That makes W.U. pretty good.
Well must stop and Get busy.
Better write me at Valentine. Expect to be back there by time you get this but if go someplace else can have my mail forwarded.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Valentine, Texas on May 5, 2917

Mr. E. H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill.
Pike County

M. W. Chandler
Valentine, Texas

Valentine, May 5th
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received Papa’s dandy letter today. Sure good to see them come so often. Hope Ralph straightens out and gives good services. I’d hate to see him get discharged. I may write JLM pretty soon and see what he can offer. Wouldn’t mind coming up to Coa if could get enough work. Think I’ll come anyway. If he will put me to work and then go to work in Western Union first time I get a chance. I’ll let you know what he says soon as I had from him. I’m getting pretty tired of this country. Easy job but don’t like the climate.
Golly prices are sure high. Darn food trusts. It’s just a drought. I’ll bet theres no good reason at all for such exorbitant prices. They just use the war as an excuse.
How’s Knox getting along. Knox why the Dicken’s don’t you write once in awhile.
Hope Margaret is well by now. Glad she didn’t get Diphtheria. I wrote Sam a letter other day. Guess he will be kinda surprised to get it. Don’t seem possible you are having so much rain there. Been wanting a rain here for last 4 months. I can’t remember when it has rained here. Everything dry as a chip. has Grace gone to Louisville yet? Gee I’d love to see Audrey.Is Lorin still selling Oliver’s?
Well i don’t know much to write.
Hope to see you all before many days.
Lovingly,
Martin
P.S. Just wrote J.L.M. for a job. Let you know what he says soon as I hear from him.

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Valentine on May 3, 1917

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike County

Valentine 5/3rd 1917
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received Papa’s letter yesterday telling about passage of Conscription law and glad to get it. Guess I’ll stay with the job for a while but I’ll be darned if I wouldn’t like to come home for a while. if I thought there was any chance of having to go to war I’d go join Navy right now cause I’d rather be in navy than in army. Gee they’re sure billing out lots of stock here. Glad I’m off this agency. Got a letter from bess other day. Guess I’ll answer it tonight. Have plenty of time on this job now. Business pretty light.
Gee it’s warm here at night now. They say mosquitoes are awful bad here in summer. Golly I’ll be it gets awful hot here in summer.
How’s Coa fixed for operations now? Wouldn’t mind having a relay job up there.
Maybe I’ll write J.L.M. for a job. I don’t like this County a bit. It’s too windy.
Well I don’t know a thing to write so will stop. Hope everybody is OK.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Bess Chandler, To: Lucerne Chandler
item.description:
From: Bess Chandler, To: Lucerne Chandler
Mailed From: Morrisonville, Illinois on January 17, 1917

Miss Lucerne Chandler
Pearl, Illinois

Dear Little Sister,
I’m sending you your Christmas gift. Hope it fits this time. I think it is real pretty.
Grace has written Mamma a letter which I’m mailing. I’m at the P.O. and just got mom’s letter and the magazine. Haven’t read letter yet. Write soon. You write such nice letters.
Lots of Love,
Bess

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Eliojah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: El Paso, Texas on June 10, 1917

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois

St. Blanca
January 10, 1917
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all;
Received 2 letters from Papa today. One via valentine and I was glad to get them both. Didn’t think you’d be able to get one to St. Blanca so quick. Nothing new to write. Getting along O.K. I called up both last night and asked them what they wanted me to do in case one called while I was working with other and they said just use my own judgement and if I pay no attention to them they get sore. I’m hitting the ball here pretty lively. Keep busy every minute of the night. The depo I trick open copied a 19 for a IP 2/5 train this pm to meet another IP No. 2 train at Fort Hancock. No. 2 got to Fort Hancock and waited 2 hours for the 2nd 5 to show up but they didn’t so he called up Dispr. on phone and went on. 2nd No. 5 was in a blind siding down the line. They claimed they didn’t get the order. Disp. came after open about it and open looked for his clearance and he had it non clearance so it will be up to the train creed.
Well, must stop. Will write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: England on January 9, 1917

Somewhere in England
Jan 9th
Dearest Folks,
Thought I’d write few lines tonight while have time but can’t tell you much except that I’m feeling OK and had a pleasant voyage.
It’s pretty cold here but not any worse than New Jersey.
Am not allowed to mention hardly anything so don’ expect to learn anything about the war from me.
Rode on an English train other night. They’re a great deal different from ours. They are built in compartments. Each compartment sealing 8 men (3rd class). No way of getting from one compartment to another except by getting off and entering another. Just like traveling in a carriage.
Had a good stateroom on the steamer and didn’t get a bit seasick.
I’ll write you again in few days and don’t worry if you don’t hear from me regularly. Hope you are all well-
Lots Love
Martin
Address Exactly Like This:
Martin W. Chandler
Co B 126 Field Bin Dig Corps
American Exp Forces

item.title: From: Grace Chandler, To: Chandler Family
item.description:
From: Grace Chandler, To: Chandler Family

Monday 8th ’17
Dearest Folks
Will try to write you a few lines this am. Was so glad to hear from Mama yesterday. Doesn’t matter to whom they are addressed, just so I get them.
Am feeling much better, one breast is still swelled, and I have the night sweats and a breaking out on my body caused from fever, But I am getting stronger every day now. Mrs. Kelley left Saturday P.M. and I bathed the baby yesterday and this morning. She is doing fine and everyone was out yesterday afternoon, then Mr. and Mrs. Geo Maxon and son wee out last night. Guess we’ll keep having company, as so many have told Lorin they’re so anxious to see the baby. He’s going to try and get some pictures of her this noon.
Thanks to Grandma Chandler, she has another silver dollar to add to her savings. Don’t think she should have done it, but we appreciate it. Lorin took her little bank up to the bank this A.M. He adds something every day I think. Mrs. Klingner and Mella were out after you left Mama and brought her a little solid gold hand ring.
The material Ruby has for her coat is so pretty and I’m sure proud of it.
Guess you’d be surprised, as we were shocked to hear Mr. Bartlett the Wabash agent here, committed suicide in the depot on Friday. No reason has been assigned to his rash act, but an auditor came in to check him up and a dray man testified at the coroners inquest that he had heard them arguing over some freight bills. Some additions that had been added to Paddock Lumber Co.’s bills. But other people think it was family affairs. Will send you the clippings from the papers if I can find them. He was the agent here for 7 years. It certainly was a shock to everyone as they were supposed to have been the happiest of families.
Am so glad to have Ruby here. She is so good to me, but I’ll tell you I missed Mama and so did Mrs. Kelley. She spoke of you so often. Bess was so sleepy after talking all night that she layer down and slept in the afternoon and I had a lump in my throat all day. Ruby had spells over the “offspring” when she arrived and has never quite gotten over her yet. Wish everyone of you could see her.
Lorin is going to be in a minstrel show tomorrow night in Taylorville , some fellows pulled out at the last minute and they asked Lorin to take one place. He’s to be an end man and has a prominent part. He’s studying his song “Are you from Dixie” and his gags. Either Bess or Ruby will go to Taylorville and see it.
Wonder what causes Mama to get so dizzy? Mrs. Kelley had those kind of spells.
Yes, we let Mrs. Wilson know you had gone. She was called to St. Louis on Friday to take care of her niece, a trained nurse, who has pneumonia and expects will be gone for some time.
Mrs. Peuce (your advisor Mama) is also very ill with pneumonia. They have a trained nurse to care for her. Other box from fathers came after such a time. He sent the baby a powder puff, me a small picture of mother and a baby, a towel, and a box of stationary, and a lot of Christmas candy. Was nice of him to remember us. He sent each member of his family something. We heard from mother , three miners and she have taken more cold and was having lots to do.
Bess and Lorin went to Bartlett’s funeral. It as held at the house hey said. There were oceans of flowers.
Will be glad to get Lucerne’s drawings . Was so sorry to her Mary school her, but its all over now and it didn’t hurt anyway did it Lucerne?
When little Jack was here, he went over to Waggners and told them we had a dog. They said “what kind of dog is it?” he said he didn’t know. They asked if it was a bird do. He said, “No! This dog don’t fly!” Ha.
Mrs. Waggner and Gladys came over the next day after you left. We have had lots of company.
Lorin just called up from town and said I had letters from home, but he had to go to Taylorvillle and won’t be back until night. Said he’d send the letters down to the school house to Bess and I’ll get them about 4 pm. I want to send this up by Bess this noon so I’ll close for this time as she’s ready to do back.
Love to Everybody,
Grace

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Sierra Blanca January 2, 1917

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill

Sierra Blanca Jan 2, 1917
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all,
Got in here last night and went to work. Job is enough to keep a man busy but not so awful hard. Have a night helper to handle baggage, etc. So I don’t have to do anything but telegraphy and clear trains on Both TP na dishes. I’m plumb disgusted with board here. This place is about the size of Hillview and only one place in town to board and they sure treat a fellow awful. Have to carry wash hater to your room and no carpet and just about the poorest accommodations a man could find. Got 1 pork chap, 2 biscuits and a few friend potatoes for breakfast and thats all. I got up from the table hungry. Charge 30.00 month. I went to bed right after breakfast this morning and got up at exactly 10 minutes after seven and they told me I was too late for supper. Had to go buy a meal at Brown’s News. They know they have a fellow cinched and they don’t care how they treat them. I asked how much for just a room and they said just the same as for board and room. Now what do you think of that? I was figuring on getting my meals at restaurant but they queered that. It’s just plain hold up. They know you can’t get any place else to stay.
If I stay here I’m sure going to get the Co to give me a box car or else build some kind of shanty and go to Baching. Can’t possibly get by for less than 35 to 40 a month for board the way it is now. If I get up after supper time I have to buy a meal and its hard to arrange sleep so can get breakfast and supper both cause I generally sleep 10 hours. Here I never eat more than 2 meals a day and they wont give me one of those if I happen to be late but they charge for it. Just the same – I told the manager what I thought abut it and he informed me I had the privilege of going some place else to board if I didn’t like it, which of course he knew I couldn’t get any place else. I’m going to every house intern tomorrow and see if I can’t get a room.
Job pays 85 don’t get the 5.00 for handling mail as the night helper does that.
Have lots trains to clear. Just twice as many as at Valentine cause here we get the Tp. trains too but don’t mind it as long as don’t have to handle baggage and mail.
Pretty cool here. They say they have cold winters here.
Well its now 11:45 s will stop and get things lined up to go to work. Work from 12 to 8.
Love to all,
Martin

item.title: From: Bess Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Bess Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Morrisonville, Ill on November 6, 1916

Mrs. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill

1:40 Sunday PM
Dearest Mama, Papa, and all
I’ve just gotten cleaned up and thought I had better write. We had intended to go to Taylorville to a football game but something was the matter with the car. I did want to go so bad, but I’m going to Jane Carrie’s house to see about a party the Glee Club is to give Thursday night.
I got along all OK with my recitation. I’ve had so many compliments on it. Nearly every time I’d see anyone who was there, they’d tell me how well I did.
You know I told you that some Taylorville Ladies came down and organized a Hilson Ladie’s Club. Well Mrs. Pence was appointed as a committee of one to arrange for a Glee Club. She asked me and six other girls and we sang here, at Harvel, and at Taylorville. Our songs were real cute. We had one to the tun of My Little Girl – Oh Mr. Hughes you’re stock are dropping
You are losing notes each day
Oh Mr. Hughes we hear you’re knocking
Tho you’re many miles away
We read your talks in all the papers
What you’ve promised not to do
Oh Mr. Hughes we know you’re lonely
But we can not note for you
We had lots of other ones too and some Wilson yells. While we were at marvel a man gave us five dollars, so were going to have a party on it. We get to invite “our company” – Don’t know who to invite. The ladies of Tayloville treated us so nice and altogether we’ve had lots of fun. We’ll know Tuesday who is to be our president.
I got my coat while I was at Taylorville. It’s brown velour. I did want a plush with brown fur trimming but they were too expensive.
Hope I get to come home Thanksgiving but guess I wont if I don’t get a pass because my fare would be nearly six dollars. I’ll sure be home Xmas tho’ and get to stay from Dec 22 to Jan.
Hope you are all well – I’m getting along fine at school. We had a program in my room day before yesterday. It was real good. The girls asked me to sin so I sang Little Gray Home in the West. We had company, too.
Lorin has just offered Grace and I $0.15 each if we read something against Wilson in the Republican news paper. You couldn’t pick up a republican news paper without reading something against Wilson. In fact that’s about all it contains.
I’m enclosing a five with which I want to pay my lodge dues for the past four or five months. Guess it wont come amiss if everything is as high as it is here. Flour is $3.00 a sack. You never did say whether or not you got the other $5.00 (which I borrowed to buy shoes in Springfield) I returned but I guess you did because you got the letter. I’ve got all of my debts paid now, Pearl Store, my board, Donohoo’s, Ruby, and you. I wrote to Mrs. Moultrie too – All I owe, now is a letter to Ruby and I’ll try to write it soon. Martin never did answer my letter. When you write tell him I’m looking for one. Lot’s of Love,
Bess

item.title: From: Grace Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Grace Chandler Gourn, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Morrisonville, Illinois on October 27, 1916

Mrs. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill

Mrs. L.E. Gourn
Morrisonville, Ill

Morrionville 10/27
Dearest Folks,
Rec’d Mama’s letter this am addressed to me and tho’t I’d write this after noon while I am resting. Washes pretty good washing this am. It is a fine bright day to dry them. Didn’t think when I got up I wanted to wash but everybody else around me was washing and just hated to see them get ahead. So Lorin stayed at home and helped me and with my electric washer and ringer was all thru by 10:30. Just got up at 7:30. Wasn’t that going some? But after I get all the scrubbing done I am pretty tired.
Lorin went in the car to Raymond this afternoon and to Nokomio if he can make it. He will be back tonight.
Sat we cleaned the house all up and washed windows inside and out. I don’t think I’ll do any general house cleaning. Washed the wood work around the windows and am going to rent a vacuum sweeper (electric) to clean the rugs and mattresses.
All of us, including Glenn, Thelma, bots, Callie, Allie and Chas were at Mother’s for dinner and supper yesterday. Had dandy meals and a good time. Bess and I went uptown Sat pm to mail that mail you received and went on down to Callie’s and she insisted on us staying for supper. Lori came home on the 6:30 train and came on down there. We stayed until 11:3. Mother send me a bunch of green tomatoes today so I’ll have to work them into pickles this week. She made some dandy chow chow.
Have brot my flower baskets inside. Think I’ll take out some of the best plants and pot them. Haven’t much room tho for flowers. That is, not a good sunny window to keep them in.
Lorin got me a nice little trimmed oak sewing chair which is very comfortable. He bronzed my old gray shoes until now they look like new.
What is the matter with Mr. Hanks that he has to be operated on? That’s too bad, hope he gets better.
Hope Martin gets to stay at the place where he is all winter. He seems to be doing pretty well.
Wonder why Bill Watters sold out in the picture show biz? Thot it was such a paying proposition? Maybe Annie was jealous of he and Roy being in together. Ha.
Glad Ruth adn Basil have gone back . The course of true love never did run smooth. Would like for her to come up and visit us. I know Bess would enjoy having her. Bess wore her new dress, hat, and shoes yesterday and looked so nice. She’s so slender. Ha. I can’t help but notice it.
Lorin has a nice new brown overcoat. He may be over there soon. I know he is going to make the territory around there either this week or next.
Wish we could come home Thanksgiving. I expect Bess will if she gets enough days off. I want her to so she can visit with you all and then tell me all about it.
Well this is all I can think of for now. Was glad to get Mama’s letter. Hope her cold is better.
Would like to get weighed, believe I am getting heavier. Bess, Lorin, and I walked up town yesterday morning before going down to mothers. Much love to all.
Write soon,
Grace

item.title: From: Grace Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Grace Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Sent From: Morrisonville on October 1, 1916

Morrisonville 10/1/16
Dearest Papa, Mama, & all: –
Guess you think it’s about time I was writing – Bess and I just got back from Sunday School. We took a spurt this am and got ready and went to the Presbyterian SS and everyone treated us so nice we are glad we went. bess is correcting some papers and making out some examination papers and I have dinner on cooking. Did think I would come in and play the graphonolia but thot I would be making better use of my time if I write home.
Ruby left yesterday morning and we sure miss her. Bess and i took her to the train, had to get up at 6 am so we could have breakfast and get to the depot by 6:58 am.
Bess and i then came home, cleaned the house real good and she had to go to a teachers reading circle at 2 pm. I dusted and scrubbed after she left took a bath and dressed up again and went to meet her. Got there in time to hear part of the work. We walked up town again went to Callie’s and she insisted on us staying and having supper. So Lorin came in on the 6:30 pm train and we went to meet him and all took supper there. Then went to the picture show. Lorin bought me the most beautiful purple velvet tricornered hat for my birthday, he said, but that isn’t until the 6th of next month. So he was in plenty of time – Ha. My white coat just got back this am from the cleaners, so you make know I wore my new hat and white coat to S.S. and felt quite dressed up. Bess cleaned her lack suit yesterday and wore my other purple hat.
Our electric washer came yesterday pm and Lorin got up early this morning and had it in working order by the time we got up. It sure us a peach and I’m tickled we have it – will sure save my back.
Lorin is going to Taylorville to get out car today, had to leave it up there the last time he was up there, on account of some man running into him and busting it up some. Will cost about $30 to get it fixed up again. Lorin sued him for $200 – the trail comes up next week. Hope he gets what it will cost us. The car is alright now so he is going to get it today.
I am cooking apples whole not peeled, with such red skin, also sweet potatoes, kraut pork & wieners. Have raw tomatoes with mayonnaise dressing for dinner.
How is papa? You said he was not feeling well when you last wrote. Hope is better by now. Guess Margaret & Lucerne will have a great time in St. Louis. Lorin said I could go, but I don’t believe I want to. It would be different if he and Bess could both go.
I was surprised Leta & John stayed in Pearl to spend their honeymoon. Guess they have gone to St. Louis by now.
Mon. P.M. Guess I’ll finish this and get it mailed. After dinner yesterday we drove to Taylorville with Oren Bloxom and another fellow, attended a football game, and drove our own car back home. Oren Bloxom came back with us – He’s a Taylorville boy, and is going to be a lawyer. Bess entertained him until his train time. I was so tired, Lorin and I went to bed. I had lunch for all.
Lorin forwarded two letters to Ruby this a.m. I told him to send them to Pearl I was afraid she wouldn’t get them if we sent them to Granite City.
I pulled the pears, Ruby will be glad to know and have just finished two gallons of pear butter. I had them on hand for over two weeks, so you may be sure I’m glad they’re cooked up.
Lorin is going to put up the base burner this afternoon. It isn’t very cold yet but he thought he’d better put it up while he had time.
Bess said at noon that she must write home. I told her I had a letter started.
She has four sets of papers to correct this evening after she comes home. She’ll be pretty busy this week with giving examinations and correcting papers.
I wish papa could come up if only for a few days, might do him good and we would be tickled to death to have him. Some of you could get a pass and come up anytime. Well this is all I can think of for now. Lorin will be down around that part of the country next week, I suppose.
Write when you can, we’re always ticked to hear from home.
Much love to all,
Lovingly,
Grace
Tues. A.M. –
Am sure going to get this mailed this morning. We have a train out of here for St. Louis at 3:37 P.M. and Lorin was just saying at the breakfast table that we could go down and see the Veiled Prophet tonight and get home on the midnight train if Bess could get her Supt. to teach for her half hour. So no telling we may be there tonight ourselves. The matter is to be settled at noon after Bess talks with the Supt. and Lorin is to study it over.
Write soon.
Grace

item.title: From: Jeanette Knox Chandler, To: Ruby D. Chandler
item.description:
From: Jeanette Knox Chandler, To: Ruby D. Chandler
Mailed From: Pearl, Illinois on September 29, 1916

Mailing Address:
Miss Ruby D. Chandler
2224 B. St.
Granite City, Illinois

Return Address:
PO Box 101
Pearl, Illinois

Pearl, Illiois, Spetmber 29, 1916
My Dear Ruby:
Just now I heard the honk, honk of an auto in front of the door but just thought it was Lewis. Then I asked Lucerne to look out and see, and it was the Smarts of Milton come down to meet May, and May was with him. She said Vinnie had sent her word to come at once as Lisa was so much worse. She asked for you and wanted you to go up with her. I wish you had been here, for it seems that none of us has been of any assistance to them. May then asked if I could jump in and go as you was not here, but of course I couldn’t leave just now, and I feed so bad about it too. And Dr. is away in hospital too, and I guess that makes Lisa feel that there is no one to look out for him. I would liked to have heard how Uncle Jim is today. Mr. Johnson was asking me how he was, and said if it hadn’t been for Aunt Sarah he wouldn’t have been down there. I told him that was the place for him for there were so many of them all there and so good to take care of him. He said if he didn’t change his mind he was going down there next Monday.
We washed today and I am tired out. Didn’t get done till after noon. I hope Aunt Sarah is feeling all right. Annie did not say in her letter but I guess if there had been anything the matter with her, she would have mentioned it. I am making corn salad now just started on it about those little onions I wrote you about. I wouldn’t get them if they are a big price. 40 per gallon is plenty to pay for them. I must stop now.
Love to all,
Mamma

item.title: From: Opal Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Opal Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Granite City, Illinois on September 21, 1916

Mrs. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois

Granite City
September 21, 1916
Dearest Net and all,
Just a few to let you know that Grandpa is better this morning. He can’t use his left hand at all. Just from his wrist. Grandma is feeling about the same. Her back and side hurts quite a bit. She wants you to send her winter underclothes and Grandpa too. We got a card from Ray on Tuesday and it was mailed at Spokane Washington. Looking for a card today. I had the paper hanger and painter yesterday. Haven’t got everything back in place yet. Was up and help Aunt clean up for she has so much to do. Bill sat up until midnight so did Sapp and Gladys. Grandpa’s bowels was so loose. Sapp got a bottle of Blackberry Brandy and it is helping him.
I bet Leta is happy. If you see give her my best wishes.
This will be all for today.
Love to all,
Opal

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Santa Margarita, CA on September 20, 1916

M.W. Chandler
Southern Pacific Company
Santa Margarita, Cal.

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill.
Pike Co.

Santa Margarita, Spet. 20
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all,
Received a letter from Papa yesterday and a long on today and was sure glad to get them. Gee they sure are doing some business back there. Think I told you in other letter I’d be here a month longer and possibly two. Glad to hear Ralph is back at work. I don’t want to work on era very bad but I’d like awful well to be closer to home. Gee I wish I could see some of you . I sold a ticket to Waterburg Conn last night – $72.40- I didn’t have any ticket on hand so I wired Sam Luis Abirro to send me one and gave him the routing and he sent it up all made out. Excursion tickets are on sale the year round. Every Friday and Saturday have reduced rates to nearly all the places along the line. Can get a ticket to Chicago and return for $65.00.
Sure have some powerful engines on this line. They’re all oil burners. Haven’t a coal burner on the line.
I stuck a first class passenger train 5 minutes yesterday morning account putting “9th” for “September” – They might give me 10 days for it – They’re awful strict. They all say that if you can work for the S.P. you can work for any road in the country. They sure enforce their rules. I was in a hurry to make out the clearance as train was ready to leave and without thinking I put 9/20 instead of September 20 – That’s OK on any other road but this one. It takes about 3 years to land a job on this road. But if extra work is good I think I’ll stick. Of course I’d probably lay off and come home before 3 years. But these are pretty good jobs and I want to land something steady if I can. I don’t have to fill lamps or lanterns or sweep out or handle baggage or anything like that. Have a baggage boy to do that. All stations have a baggage boy. All I have to do is sell tickets, copy orders, and put on mail. Sure copy a bunch of orders and seek quite a few tickets.
Well must stop. Hope to hear from you all soon-
I’ll write more often
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Opal Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
item.description:
From: Opal Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
Mailed From: Granite City, Illinois on September 19, 1916

Mrs. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois

Granite City
September 19, 1916
Dearest Net and all,
Just a few lines to tell you Grandpa is awful sick. Had the Dr. to him today. Grandma isn’t feeling very well either. The Fall didn’t put her in bed but made her feel bad. Grandpa told Bill he didn’t think he could last long. The rest of us are all well. So glad you got to go to the fair. Bill is waiting for this to close.
As ever,
Opal

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Santa Margarita, CA on September 18, 1916

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois
Pike Co

Santa Margarita Sept 18th
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received Mama’s letter yesterday and haven’t heard from papa in a coons age. Sure was glad to get Mama’s letter. This is first time I’ve written for several days. Getting along OK and will be on this job at least a month longer and probably 2 months. Agent has gone to New York so regular 3rd trick man got his job leaving me here for while longer. Sure have a bunch of train orders to handle. Keeps me going sometimes. Getting pretty cool out there at night. Have to have a fire every night. See in the paper where they have rented the M.E. Church for Primary room. Thought they had built a new school house there or had added to the old one. See they’ve started on the ditch again. I’d like to see it.
I’ve been going up to the school-man’s house nearly every night. We all went swimming other day. Gee they have swell schoolhouse here. Have piano, dance floor, opera house, and everything in it. Have some pretty swell scenery on the stage. It’s a single story building but has 4 rooms besides the opera and dance room. Sure is swell.
Gee I sure was tickled when agent told me he was going to lay off 2 months. Felt pretty sure I’d get to stay on this job. Ruby is making a pretty good visit at Grace’s. Wish I was there.
Well I must stop and get busy. Bell rings just about every 10 or 15 min for 9.00. Wish you’d all write a little more often.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Richard Knox Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Richard Knox Chandler
Mailed From: Santa Margonita, Cal. on September 3, 1916

Mr. Richard Knox Chandler
Pearl, Ill.
Pike County

Santa Margonita
Sept. 3
Dear Little Hi-Pockets
By Golly you waited an awful long time before you answered my letter. What seems to be the trouble? Anyway I was awful glad to get it. Aren’t you glad to get started back to school?
Golly you misspelled lots of words and used a good deal of rough grammar. But seeing that you’ve been out of school quite a bit I’ll excuse you this time. But never again.
Are you and the little Hoover girl still chummy? Golly I wish you were out here with me. Did you and Dick Davis wrestle any? i’ll bet he can work on you.
Well old timer. I got a train close so must stop. Now since you are starting to school you will have plenty of paper and pencils and you can write to me every day or so.
Your Great Big Brudder,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Santa Margarita, California on August 16, 1916

Mrs. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill.
Pike Co

Santa Margarita Aug 16
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received Mama’s nice long letter today and the “Tribune” and “Times” from Bess and sure glad to get them. It’s the first I’ve received for a week. Haven’t heard from Papa for about a week. Generally hear from Papa every 2 or 3 days. Not much news to write. Received letter from Ruth Powers yesterday. She is going to Fairmount College this winter. Surprised to hear Carrie Wild was married. I received 2 or 3 letters from her while in Montana but she didn’t say anything about being engaged. Got my pay check yesterday. $49.00. Board was 27 and O.R. 2 $6.00 and paid $5.00 on my suit. Got $3.50 left. I’m going to send for Tribune tonight so can get it every week. It’s getting a little colder here all the time. Have to have a fire every night. Think I’ll be here until first of September. Bulletin was up on this place yesterday but don’t think they will fill it until 1st of month. Sure hope they don’t strike cause that would throw us out of a job. I don’t think they will strike though. I went to Atascadero yesterday pm with another man and his wife in a car. It’s a settlement just sprung up lately. Yet it sure is a pretty place. More like a park than anything else. All kinds flowers. We have lots of fruit of every description here. I’m so tired of it can hardly look at it anymore. Here Knox sure pulled off a heroic stunt when he saved the little girls fishing pole. Ha- wish I could see you all. I was so homesick last night didn’t know what to do. I’d just love to see that Illinois river.
Must stop and go to work.
Write Often
Love to all,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Santa Margarita, CA on August 9, 1916

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike Co

Santa Margarita 8/9 1916
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received letter from Papa yesterday and sure glad to get it. Nothing new to write. Getting along OK. It has been pretty cool here last 2 days. Had to build fire last night and got one going tonight. All the people around here treat me just fine.
Mama I haven’t received the pictures yet. Will enclose stamps to send them. Would like to have the Tribune occasionally too. I’m going to to subscribe for it pretty coon. Was intending to go swimming today but it was too cold. Played ball with Santa Margarita last Sunday and guess will play again next Sunday.
I’m feeling pretty bum today. Caught a bad cold but guess I’ll be ok in day or two. Well must stop as don’t know anything to write. Everybody write soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Denison, Texas on February 19, 1916

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois
Pike Co.

Denison, Tex. 2/18
Dearest Folks,
Arrived there last night and went to work this am. Been all day checking the place up. Had over 1000.00 worth commisionary goods. Sure am tired tonight. Got a letter from Sam yesterday – said you were worrying cause I hadn’t been writing. Having sweep weather another month with bring the summer.
Sure got a lot of work ahead of me to get straightened out. Guess I’ll be OK in couple days though.
This job pays $30.00 and board. If I stay here this summer will be getting 40 by then.
Only have 30 men in this gang. I have to keep track of their meals and purchases and charge them for it. Sales amounted to 18.00 yesterday. Will get my first pay the 15th of March. Have about $12.00 coming. Sure going to try and save a little if I can. May stay with this job for quite awhile and again may not. Tell better when summer comes.
Well will close-feel awful sleepy.
Sure like to hear from all of you often.

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Denison, Texas on February 7, 1916

Mr. E. H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike Co

M. Chandler
K18 Denison, Tex

Denison, Feb 5
Dearest Folks,
Gee wish I hadn’t told you not to write sure miss the mail. Expected to get out by first of month but account of work closing down on Union Pacific all the men came down here so I may be here a week yet. want you all to write me right away. Am enclosing letter from Ft. Worth so you see I can’t tell exactly when I will get out. Having pretty good time. Gained 12 pounds since being down here and feel fine. Sure have good meals.
I put out pretty good washing today. Washed bed clothes beside my clothes. Last 5 days sure have been swell. Couldn’t ask for better weather. I’m 5 miles out from Denison now but still get mail at Denison-K-18-
You just keep on writing and if I leave I can have it forwarded. Hope everybody is well. Is Ruth still there?
Well I don’t know hardly anything to write so will close.
Hope to hear from all of you soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Hillsboro, Texas on January 14, 1916

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike Co

Hillsboro, Tex Jan 14, 1916
Dearest Folks,
Thought I’d write few lines this am. I’ve been going on so much about how warm it was and night before last it dropped to 10 degrees about zero. I was in a box car all night and it was certainly cold. I didn’t go to Greenville with Mr. Coster as expected. Stayed in San Antonio another day trying to get a job. I came to Hillsboro and have been treated fine. The above company have their bunk cars here and they have me my meals and the foreman gave me a splendid letter to W.L. Hilt to help me towards getting a job. Says it don’t pay very much to start but good chance for promotion for right man. Sure have reacted me like a prince. I’ll go from here to Dallas and then to Greenville to get my clothes and then to Ft. Worth to see this company. Ft. Worth is close to Dallas but will have to go to Greenville to get my clothes account can’t have them forwarded. With the letter I have, I certainly ought to be able to get something. Will send you a copy of the letter. It is about 20 degrees above zero this am and am sure glad I’ve a good warm place to stay while I’m here.
This Mr. Allen who gave me the letter hadn’t know me but about 5 hours when he gave it to me. Sure is a nice man.
Well I’ll write you soon as get to Ft. Worth and see what I can get. Hope everything is well and OK.
Lovingly,
Mart

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: New Orleans, LA on December 25, 1915

Mrs. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ills
Pike County

New Orleans Dec 25th
Dearest Folks,
Sure don’t seem like Christmas. Leave here this pm. Probably be in Houston Tuesday or Wednesday unless land something before I get there. Lots of great sights here. Went through Louisiana State Museum yesterday evening. Sure interesting. Was also down to Wharves where they were unloading cargo of bananas. Will write again soon.
Martin

item.title: From: J.M. Jones, To: Grace Chandler
item.description:
From: J.M. Jones, To: Grace Chandler
Mailed From: St. Louis on June 19, 1913

Oliver Type Writer Building
812 Pine Street.
St. Louis
June 19/1913

Miss Grace Chandler,
Pearl, Illinois

Dear Miss:
We are in receipt f your letter of June 18th in which you have asked for commissions due on sale to J.W. Smith and H. Owings.
The commission on the order of J.W. Smith is due, and check is being sent you under separate cover today.
The commission on the sale to Herbert Owings will not be due until April 7th, 1914, at which time you will receive your commission check in accordance with the contract which was made with you.
Yours very truly,
J.W. Jones
Assistant Manager

item.title: From: Unknown, To: Grace Chandler
item.description:
From: Unknown, To: Grace Chandler
Mailed From: Pearl, Illinois on November 28, 1912

My Dear Gracie,
Not so much fun about that as there was in the beginning of your letter. But then the old era is so darn full of trains tonight, I had to come down and relieve the Opr tonight, while he went to dinner Ha. First my dear I want to mention tomorrow night. This weather one “guy” can’t have much luck on a speeder and that way I’d have to come over if I came. So if all is suitable with you I’d rather make it Friday instead of Thurs eve and I’ll come on 33 and back on the Chicago train and that way you’ll not have to ask me to leave at ten for I’ll have to go shortly before. Grace you know those trains are always some last an I’ll get to stay until your tired of me. Yes about your friend Mr. Lienhatrdt, I sat with him coming home on 12 Monday. He also told me he was with you at a party other night. made me kinda sore too cause I never get any invitations to the parties. Ha. Yes it was really me he saw on 12 – true I would have enjoyed a couple of days more at home but my dear there is seemingly no rest in sight and I must also add that truly, the most restful periods in my “career” is, when I am spending my evenings with you. And I look forward anxiously to those evenings. I wonder if I will be fortunate enough to spend a few more of them.
Yes! When you mentioned that great subject (candy), seems to me as though I can recall a bet made some weeks ago, where in you were looser? And am counting big on tasting some real good fudge when you make it. Do remember me.
And you are contemplating going to St. Louis eh! Looks like you’d put it off until next Saturday night and let me go along. We will take in a show and look around some. Honest – for I need to do the shopping stunt too.
Here’s my trip Saturday- to Maybrew on 15- Marshall on 18 Sunday Slater on 24 Sunday-12 onto Roadhouse and back on 19- 8:30 am – Monday. Had a great time, met some dandy fellows at Marshall, also saw some girl friends. Wish you might have been along for Missouri (Saline County) is the place for fun. Ask “Jake” will mail this on #15 tomorrow and trust it will reach you in due time also meet your approval.
Let here have a card on 16 dearie if ok for me to come up Friday evening.
Darn if we have been together for 4 months. Save me a kiss too will you? French? Yes.
You going to meet the train – 33? yes. No news here so I will leave it with you. Too bad about Smith. Ha.
All yours,
(Unreadable Scribble)
8:30 1st Wednesday

item.title: From: Ruby Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Ruby Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Wichita, Kansas on October 23, 1912

Wichita, Kansas October 23, ’12
Dearest Papa, Mamma, and All:
We received the children’s and Papa’s letters yesterday, Mamma’s registered and Bess’ letters today so I feel especially good tonight.
I was awfully glad to get the $15.00 for Martin’s suit. Will order it Saturday, then he’ll get it in a week. After this month thought I will have gotten a good start and wont be so hard pressed for extra coin. We’ll get a pay day a few days earlier this month on account of the Topeka trip. Say Papa I wish you’d order it right away for Ill need it the 6th and thats a short time off. order it Via Rock Island as a special is chartered for the benefit of Wichita teachers and promises to get us there in about 14 and a half hours.
I was glad Bess sent that music. I have those two you mentioned but can’t locate the song book. Will tell you later what I do and what happens.
Bess, I was rather depending on you ordering my hat thru Edna, since you were going to pay me a little on my coat than $5.00. But if you can’t share it, I can wait until I get my next pay and get it here the day before I go to Topeka for I can’t get it right now.
Form the way your letters read it seemed you didn’t get my last one for in it I asked about my hat and told you what I wanted also told Mamma on back of envelope it was ok about bed trade.
If you can’t order hat thru Edna I’ll first get a sailor for I’d have to pay a sum for beaver and trim it like I want it. Ethyl and I rented a piano and it was moved in last Sat. so I feel so much more at home. I was first crazy about before I got it. I sure will put in the time. Martin learned to play “Rock of Ages” clear thru with both hands. He’s awfully proud of it. ha! He’s onto Mae’s now. I had to go to Teacher’s Association and a dinner afterwards so he went out there. I had him go to a “Delicatessen” right near us, for his supper and go out there afterwards. I haven’t seen her since Sunday but called her up this noon and she said she’d be down after school tomorrow. I did quite a washing last night and ironed this a.m. before I went to school so as to be ready for that down tonight. I wore my white veil and a tight red low made from the ribbon on my summer hat, put it right in the back. It looked good. I had several compliments. You know, my veil dress split in 3 or 4 places and I took it to Boston Store and showed them and they gave me $2.50 due bill for material. So I got a wide insertion and set it in which also lengthened it just enough. I’m quite proud of my handiwork. I still have $1.00 of that left. Not in money but due – bill. It will come in handy sometime.
I am going to a show this week and wear my light blue dress. Ethyl had a fit over it. I agent been ad it on yet. I will be the first show I have seen, not even the princess. Sam is join got take me to Forum Friday night.
I’m glad Grace got her a traveling bag. One needs it so often. Mine will come in handy at Topeka. Say, I fixed my blue dress up dandy so I can wear it all winter. I cleaned it and pressed it and put the waist back on so it looks most as good as new. I’ll clean my lavender so I can take both to the convention.
Say, I have got a peachy coat. It’s a mixture and has big lapels of broadcloth. It’s as swell as any I’ve seen. It’s the bicle cloth, pretty rough mostly black, so a black hat will go well with it. Bess did you get your grey beaver trimmed with pink. I saw one down town, and it would be so pretty for you.
Grace are you wearing your suit or your cast winter coat? You didn’t mention so I wondered. Your blue suit was pretty on you.
The children’s letters were so cute. I can read them over and over and laugh every time. It sure tickles Martin to hear what Knox says. He says “Don’t you wish we had him here.” I have thought so often how much good it would do one of the little girls here with we while they were out of school so long. I want them to have music so bad. After awhile I’m going to ave Martin play. He wants to so bad and it seems easy for him.
I forgot to tell you how I paid for my coat. Why since I’m a teacher I can run a bill, so whatever is absolutely necessary I can get there anytime. It came in handy for I needed it so bad when I got my dresses, I still wear my suit lots but its so hard to keep my waist ironed. I had them rough dried at the Steam Laundry also sheets, pillow cases and table cloths and Martin’s collars, came to $0.47. I’m going to have them laundered every 2 weeks, then do my own ironing. It’s sure worth that much and more to have them clean.
I have some of the cutest pictures Mae and I made. Cut out magazine pictures and pasted them on gown mats. Some are of Sat. evening pasts. Adds lots to my room.
I made some dandy corn fritters for supper last night and had some left for dinner today. It’s so handy having some thing already fixed for quick brunch at work. The mail usually comes at noon and I have a time popping from stove to letters getting them read.
I’ll sure take time to write Aunt Sarah later also to Pearl. Girls I’ve had several cards from Irvin Pounds with his address – gentle hint! Guess I’ll write him too.
