You’ve asked so many time about color of Martin’s suit and I forget to answer. He wants brown mixture and its very popular too. A sort of red brown then he wants brown shoes before he comes home so of course I’ll be able to get them then. He takes real good care of his appearance – as good as possible. He can spend a good deal time at Mae’s or over to Sam’s (he usually does) while I am at Topeka and sorts rough about for his meals down here. I feel safe enough about leaving him so much with Sam. They’re pretty good roomies. And he likes Mrs. D.D. too she jollies with him so much. Don’t mention anything about being afraid to leave him in your letters but you might tell him to make the best of everything while I’m away. I know where he is every minute for he gets out a certain time and I know he doesn’t waste much getting here. he looks fine and never coughs one, since he had that cold.
Grace, it’s about time you were writing again. I’d like to write lots more but will have to go to bed its 11:20 and I was up late last night. Guess I’ll write on the other side tho. Say Mrs. Mussenbach must want her fame as a poctiss to spread abroad. I saw two in the paper last week. Guess I’ll send Carrie a card, and put my address on it. Hers is just Woodriver but I’ll put c/o Washington School, Cleveland Ave.
I’m rather anxious to know the outcome of the settlement, so is Mae. Art asked Mae what she was going to do with her half. He’s pretty busy making Xmas presents. Guess he don’t want the worry of it right at the last. Must close. Write as often as you can. It’s a deal to look forward to after school hours to expect mail. I think thats why Martin rushes home so.
Love to All,
Ruby

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family

Mailing Address:
Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois
Pike County

Return Address:
M. Chandler
COB 1st BSC
Mammouth Parking

9 am Indianapolis, Mo. 18th
Dearest Papa, Mama, & all
En route to Mammouth Park, Mo. Cmae through K.C. & St. Louis both but was only in each place 15 minutes and was way down in yards. We weren’t allowed to leave train at all. Just now pulling into Maple. Intended to write you from KC but no chance. We came through St. Louis at 11 pm last night. Rock bends El Paso to St. Louis and then St. Louis to destination. Should reach New Jersey about night. All the trains are taking siding for us and we have had a clear track since leaving Mt. Bliss. Delayed occasional by broken tunnel on one of the car horses and then we have to unload them every 3 hours and let them rest 8 hours. All the little towns in Missouri and Kansas had word of our coming and school was dismissed and they were all down to station with flags to wave at use. One girl passed out a basket of cigarettes. from way they are rushing us am inclined to think we will go on over to France although some say we are going to camp in NJ for winter. We have dandy pullman and good meals. Having fine trip. Didn’t come through Wichita. Wanted to bad too. Came through Hutchinson, Kans. Well I’m in hurry so can mail this here in Maples cause don’t know when we will stop again. Will write you just as soon as get to New Jersey and give you my address.
Love to all
Martin
(over)
P.S.
Suppose you get the Battalion picture my picture isn’t a bit good. Can hardly be recognized. Am in the sixth grow from the right and third row right next to the big black horse on cart.

item.title: From: Pearl Ellis, To: Ruby Chandler
item.description:
From: Pearl Ellis, To: Ruby Chandler
Mailed From: Manchester, Illinois on January 19, 1911

Miss Ruby Chandler
Pearl, Illinois
Pike County

Thady’s Farm
Jan 18 – 1911
My dear Ruby,
Are you paying me back for the way I treated you dear? Well I don’t like it. I want to hear from you. Did you ever get my photo I sent to you before Christmas? I was afraid you had not, as I had not heard from you. How is everybody? Give my love to all the family. I was at Knox’s last Sunday. They are all well. Am getting a little tired of school. Had a fine time in Decater and Urbana during holidays.
Love,
Pearl

item.title: From: Vinnie, To: Margaret Knox
item.description:
From: Vinnie, To: Margaret Knox
Mailed From: Milton, Ill. on February 14, 1907

Miss Margaret Knox
Pearl, Ill.
Grover is here had to resend letter. He has his money.

Milton, Ill. Feb 13, ’07
Dearest Margaret,
Here is the three dollars – all of Grover’s currency that I know anything about. Wish I could see you to have a long talk. Find out, if you can, where he is going. I don’t know what he means by the way he is acting. He don’t seem to know himself. I am busy today making wigs for the play. I think it will be real good, Bro Campbell stopped in this a.m. and volunteered to begin church earlier so we could begin out play at 8. You know we are having a big meeting. Sixteen were baptized Mon. night. Our new piano is just grand. Some of the “cranks” call it “Mrs. Allen and Johnston’s piano.” We don’t care for we want them all to know how hard we worked for it. We have special music every night and really I never heard such sermons as Rev. Campbell preaches. They say he is the best preacher that was ever in our pulpit. I love him as a man too – He is so good. We are all getting along fine and are happy. Oh I could tell you so much, if I could see you. I’m happiest really than I’ve been for three years. I have certainly had a steady job tending the phones for a long time and at home class, but I’m only glad to do it, as Doc seems so much better satisfied when he knows I’m at the phone to answer the calls. Asa is doing fine. He has been so good to me and is really doing fine. Well Dearie it is time to go practice so I’ll have to quit. If you answer of course, you know enough not to mention about me referring to our happiness, but I know we all are come up when you can. Write and tell me all about Jess and everybody. Tell Aunt Nettie I’ll write to her soon and that I am not angry. No – why should I be – I write about as often as she does after all – thats not at all.
My arm is so sore I can hardly write at all.
From your friend,
Vinnie

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: McNary, LA. on December 29

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill.
Pike Co.

Dearest Folks,
Was out of post cards and couldn’t write. This is first place I’ve stopped off since leaving New Orleans. Will be in Houston Friday. Sure am anxious to get there so can get my mail. Would liked to have sent something to you all for Xmas but couldn’t. Railroads down here pay pretty good wages but plenty of men will be leaving here pretty soon. This is just small place. Have saw mill here.
Am enclosing a handkerchief for Mama. Wish I could have sent something better for your birthday. Will write again soon. Sure would like to get a job. Hope you are all well.
Love to all,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Cairo, Ill. on December 16

Cairo, Ill. Dec 16
Dearest Folks,
Getting along OK. Leave here today. Sure hope I can get a job. it’s pretty cold down here but don’t mind it much. Rather be traveling this way than to be laying round in Pearl. Sure would like to hear from yours. I can imagine what you all think of me for leaving this way especially while Grace and Lorin were there but think I’d rather be most anywhere than Pearl.
Next time I write I’ll give you an address and want to hear from some of you.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin W. Chandler, To: Pike County Republican
item.description:
From: Martin W. Chandler, To: Pike County Republican
Mailed From: Pearl, Illinois on November 21

Mailing Address:
Pike County Republican
Pittsfield, Illinois

Return Address:
Martin Chandler
Pearl, Illinois

Enclosed herewith forty cents in stamps for which please mail eight copies of the Nov. 16th issue of the Republican, containing obituary of E.H. Chandler. Also, will you please return letter addressed to “Bro. Reavis” and signed “W.H. Garrison” pertaining to Mr. Chandler’s death. Letter was sent to you along with obituary on the 11th inst.
Very truly,
M. W. Chandler
Pearl, Illinois

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Little Silver, New Jersey October 18

Oct 18th
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received papas letter yesterday and Bess’ dandy letter today and mighty glad to get them. I came over other night and wrote but forgot to mail it so guess it has been quite a while since you’ve heard from me. The 11th Reserve battalion left for France this morning. We got our lockers back this am also got stoves so guess we will camp here this winter from looks of things but of course can’t tell for sure. I think they intended to send one battalion over and hadn’t decided who to send hence our preparedness but now since the 11th have gone we’re likely to stay here for some time. I’ve been getting the Pike Country Republican lately. Who’s sending it? It has news from boys at Camp Taylor. Saw Wade’s and Jesse’s picture in it.
Tell Parish I’ll write the Tribune a letter relative Army Life as far as I knew. Don’t know anything about it except Signal Corps Branch. Awful glad to hear Knox’s arm is healing. Hope he doesn’t fall from some place and break it again before it mends. We’ve been out on target range 3 days out of this week and go again tomorrow. I can shoot pretty well. Scored 76 out of 100 first time. I even tho one of the automatic pistols. Lots pretty good shots in this company. Is Aunt Sarah still at our house?
They are offering liberty bonds to our company on installment plans. We have about 75 men and they’re taken $4200.00 so far. I can’t take any account the allotment home. Have o pay at rates $10.00 per month and thats all I’m getting. By the way, you’ll get first payment 1st of December. Captain said it was paid one month behind June all the time and then you’ll get the last one a month after I’m out of army. Gee Margaret is getting rather popular. Having bunch of fellows wanting to call on her.
It’s pretty chilly here. heavy frosts each morning. Well I’ll stop now and go back to camp. Pretty tired tonight. On our feet all day today fixing stoves for the company. Will write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Annie, To: Jeanette and All
item.description:
From: Annie, To: Jeanette and All
Sent From: Granite, September 25

Dear Nett and all,
I will write you a few lines. Pa is lots better today. He is sitting up was out in front room this morning for quite a while. Martin had a letter to answer and share him so he looks better and he says he feels better. He is awful weak but can help himself so much better than he did. He started a line last night and I got up and mailed it. Him and me get along fine. Virginia is on my lap she wanted to know who I was writing to. She said do you want Aunt Nett will come down.
Well I will close
Love to all,
Annie

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Unknown Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Unknown Female Chandler
Mailed From: Santa Margarita, CA on September 3

Santa Margarita, CA Sept 3
Dear Little Sister,
Got your letter this morning together with Margaret’s and was sure glad to get it. By golly I wish you’d all write every day. Hang on to the iron kiddo. It will make a woman out of you. Gee that sure was a whole bunch of tough luck about that earache. Did you try warm milk and Laudanum? That’s what Mama used to do for me when I was a kid. You want to read slow on this so it will last longer cause I haven’t got time to write very much.
Well sweetheart the strike “haint” going to be pulled off so guess I’ll work a while longer.
I sent Margaret 3 Simoleans to buy books. Forgot about her birthday Aug 26 but I’ll try and remember March 10th.
Suppose you’ve been living in joyful anticipation of the coming Monday whence you will again enter the old school house. Well I gotta stop.
Write me right away quick,
Yrs,
Martin

item.title: From: Ruby Chandler, To: Grace Chandler
item.description:
From: Ruby Chandler, To: Grace Chandler
Mailed From: Wichita, Kansas on September

Wichita, Kans. Sept
Dearest Grace;
Received your care today and was glad to get a line from you. Will send picture inclosed later. I brought it down from Mae this evening.
We are quite comfortably located now, will proceed to desirable rooms as near as possible. The room facing Cleveland Ave has one window on that side and one at the end. Have Mae’s sanitary couch at that window – on the north that is – and the dresser in the corner. Have a white iron bed at the other end of room, a table in the center and a gas heater and two rockers, the other room is same size with one large window, and the entrance door, with a closet leading off. A fine place for my clothes and shelves for my hats. Have a dandy gas stove and over a kitchen cabinet with top, which I use for the dishes, a square dining table and the chairs, and a nice rug on both floors.
Mae and Art came up for supper, we had watermelon for desert. You never saw such big melons there and the biggest are $0.15. A $0.10 one was plenty and had some left and just think how much Martin and I eat. Say anything you want to do. Wont insult us a particle.
How I do wish it were possible for you to be here with me then I’d board you so you could go to business college too. There’s a discount for two from same family.
I can swim to beat the dutch. Breast stroke and on my back, too. We all went this am quite a crowd there. Sam took me boat riding the other night and asked me last night to go again so you can bet I will. Haven’t been to any shows yet, don’t expect to for quite a while.
11 am Came up to Mae’s after my work was done and I sent Martin for his books. He will go down to the college in the morning to get ready for Mon. I’ll have to go to another teacher’s meeting in the morning until noon.
I’ll be glad when we both get started so we can keep busy. Received Grace’s letter this am and I was so glad, had to shed a few tears.
I just love the place where I stay, but I’ll have to get used to the surroundings before I feel at home.
What was some of the music Mr. Gorin sent you? Mrs. Davis has several of the new ones we knew.
Mae has a new vacuum cleaner just like ours. Martin sleeps on the sanitary couch and I used the iron bed. Plenty of room for a sister Ha.
I must quit so I can get your picture wrapped.
Mae had three peach trees just loaded with Alberta peaches and such big ones. This is the first year they’ve borne fruit.
I’ll be anxious to hear from you so write.
Much love to all,
Ruby

item.title: From: May, To: Margaret Knox
item.description:
From: May, To: Margaret Knox
Mailed From: Milton, Ill on August 81, 1900

Miss Margaret Knox
Pearl, Ill

Return in 5 days to
F. Johnston, M, D.,
Milton, Ill.

Milton, Ill.
Aug, 30, 1900
Dearest Aunt,
I’m here and sick as usual, but not nearly so sick as I usually get. I didn’t “puke” at all but was feeling mighty bad , had such a terrible headache.
I forgot the black collar which belongs to my organdy dress and you send it by Mr. Lester tomorrow (Friday). It is in the top of my bunk just raise the lid and you’ll see it. Tell Ruby that Veda has been over already to see if she was coming back.
Aunt Helen has been in to hear about Ace.
This is all the news at present. Haven’t been out any yet.
Write to me soon,
Your Niece,
May

item.title: From: Elijah L. Fhurst, To: Margaret M. Knox
item.description:
From: Elijah L. Fhurst, To: Margaret M. Knox
Mailed From: Pittsburg, Ill. on August 7, 1900

Miss Margaret M Knox
Pearl, Ill.

Dear Friend,
Replying to your freight data which I hadn’t answered on account of absence from home. I will say that you should accept the amount sent you but do not receipt in full of your claim for it.
I am going to Springfield soon and when there will look the matter up for you. It seems that your claims should have been paid in full on account of your with drawl from the association when you did. When I go to Springfield will write you. (Hurrah for Libby and Horrshumin) –
Yours very truly,
Elijah L. Fhurst

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Santa Margarita, CA on July 22

Santa Margarita
July 22nd
Dearest Papa and All,
Just received letters from you, mama, Lucerne and Margaret fe minutes ago and was sure glad to get the. Wish they would come that way all the time. I wrote yo Mama few minutes ago and wrote to her day before yesterday in Morrisonville so guess she will get it soon after she gets there.
Getting along OK on the job. Coping about 50 train orders last night and had 43 Expense Bills. Handle mail or 3 trains and sell tickets for 3 trains so there’s generally enough to keep me busy. Like the job fine though. Theres lots of fellows here wanting to lay off and can’t get relief. M en are awful scarce but in the winter time they close so many offices that it throws a whole bunch of men on extra board but extra work looks pretty good for this winter and if I earn to handle an agency by that time will be assured of almost steady work. These agencies pay big money too. Do you and Knox get any fish? That was a pretty good string you caught the other day. Bet Knox was tickled to yank them out.
Wish I was there so could go squirrel hunting few times. Gee the girls sure are bathing lots berries. Hope Ruby is feeling better. Golly I haven’t heard a piano for so long I’ve forgotten how one sounds. Hope Ralph will be able to go back to work soon. Too bad Micky had to take sick.
Well the train is coming now that I want to get this off on so will close. Wish all of you would write. Hope everyone is OK. Will send Annie a card right away.
Love to all,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin W. Chandler, To: John, Bess, and all
item.description:
From: Martin W. Chandler, To: John, Bess, and All
Mailed From: Sandpoint, Idaho on July 1

Dear John, Bess, and All
I’ve been threatening to write for the past three weeks and guess I’ll get it down right now. We had quite a trip up this way. Made good time after leaving Lincoln. Another fellow and myself left the 40 and 8 camp the first of June. There was nothing around Chao in the way of work and we thought we’d come up here and prospect, expecting first to find some kind of job so we could get equipment to go into the hill with but work sure is scarce around this country and there are thousands and thousands of men up this way looking for work. Not exaggerating, there were at least 200 men on every freight train we rode this side of Omaha. Also saw several women riding the box cars. They climb right in with a gang of men in a box car and I guess that’s their safest bet.
We’re camping here on a big lake. Have been for two weeks. Got a little hut of pine boughs and we catch more fish than we can eat. The lake is entirely surrounded by mountains and sure is pretty.
Guess we’ll stay here until the forest fires break out and then everybody will get a job. They say we can expect the first to start anytime now and the government hires every available man to fight ’em. I hear a person can earn anywhere from $25.00 up to $400.00, depending on duration of fire. The pay is $0.25 per hour, including Chuck, and your time usually runs about 20 hours a day. I’ll certainly be glad to earn enough to pay the bills at Carroll and the ambulance and Doctor at Dunlap. It makes me heart sick to think of those bills and I suppose you folks are getting plenty of duns. Just as soon as I can possibly earn some dough I’ll shoot it down that way. I thought at first that i’d stay at the 40 and 8 camp and be able to pay $15 a month on my debts but they only allow a man 30 days in camp now because there are so many waiting to get in.
We came up through Sheridan, Wyo. Billings and Helena, Mont. and stopped off at Trout Creek, Mont., for couple days to fish. We went into mountains and camped by a dam nice trout stream but nights were too cold and we had no blankets. It was a real pretty place to camp, with a good spring close by and I’m going back there some day and camp a week or two. The first night we were there I got up about 1 am and built a big fire cause twas too cold to sleep. Then about 3:30 am, just as it was commencing to get day light, I went down to the spring for some water to make coffee. There was some kind of an animal at the spring getting a drink. Don’t know what it was but think it was a young bear. It scurried away before I got a good look at it. If it had just stayed a second longer, I’d have done enough scurrying for both of us.
We catch lots of trout, Crappie, and Perch out of this lake and its a big help, as it takes care of the meat problem, I wish I had a Kodak.
There’s some right pretty scenery around here.
I was out on a log boom fishing other day and fell into lake. No damage done except to my temper. The lake water is as clear as a crystal and about 40 feet deep.
Well guess I’ll call this a letter and seal it up. I’m feeling great. Haven’t been troubled any with my ulcer for past 6 weeks. Hope this finds all of you ok and that you have a good crop of corn.
Address me here.
Lovingly,
Mart

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: France on June 26th

France June 26th
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all,

item.title: From: Grace Chandler, To: Ruby and All
item.description:
From: Grace Chandler, To: Ruby Chandler and All
Mailed From: Morrisonville on June 5

Morrisonville 6/5
Dearest Ruby & all: –
Well I’ll bet you’ll think of all things! To actually get a letter from me – I certainly have been neglectful but I hope you’ll forgive and forget the laps of time since I last wrote.
Of course you know I have the baby and besides being chief cook and Bottle Washer, it keeps myself pretty busy.
The girls arrived OK and we were so glad to see them, and they I think were overjoyed to see us and up to PM the present time 10:30 are still having fits over the baby. She does so many cute things. We can’t tell you all, but you will see when we come over. Mr. Smith is calling on Bess tonight. We have all just been up town in the car and had ice cream sodas. We also met the girls in the car. I’m so afraid it’s going to rain tonight so we can’t go in the car. We are all evicted down to mothers tomorrow for dinner. Bess will go to the city I guess about Thursday and Lucerne says she is going with her, but that wont be much of a visit. I made bread today for the first time since I was married and it was just lovely. The girls thot it was fine. We have been having strawberries pretty often. Had them tonight. Was too bad about Uncle Geo, wasn’t it? So sad for Aunt Annie. Am glad Mama went out there. I’ll bet it will be rather lonesome for you Ruby without the girls away. But Bess will woo be home. Gee! I sure do hate to see her leave. Don’t suppose she will be home long either as she is going to big college this summer. Ruby you know how it is for me to write now. Wasn’t to talk to the girls. So will tell you goodnight tonight. Hope Papa is well and the rest. Will write soon again-
Love to all,
Grace

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: France on April 11

France April 11th
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
No mail since last writing. Received letter from Bess today dated at Dunlap. Sure was glad to get it. That’s letter number 3 received since being here. Nothing new to write, or rather, lots news to write but can’t write it. Having lovely weather. Guess Aunt Anna and Ruby are there now. Bess said they were going to meet in K.C. and come to Pearl together.
I’d like to be there myself. Am still batching with other fellows. Like it fine. I’m on a Radio job here. Get Paris and Berlin press each day. Get about 1000 words from Paris relative military situation. German don’t put out much news.
I’m getting fleshy on our own cooking. Most meals consist of Ouefs, Pomme de terries, Coffee, Bun de pain, and confiturerie.
You see I’m learning to cook in the French style-Ha. We only have 2 meals a day – one about 10:30 am and one about 5:00 pm. We 5 fellows sure have a great time. At least we enjoy ourselves as much as possible under the existing conditions. Lots singing, joking, etc. Might win myself a home with a little French girl if I could speak and understand French well enough. I get a smile once in a while and then when she starts talking I’m lost so then she gets peeved cause all her words were wasted. Sure is a great life. We have things fixed pretty nice in our radio station. Good bunks, etc.
Dad how goes everything on the “only way”? Did you all get a new schedule yet? They should get a raise by all means. We have a sergeant in charge of this station. Sure is a Prince besides a very efficient man. If I ever get a chance I’ll have some pictures taken and send home. Intended doing it before leaving the states. Hows fishing around there? I haven’t seen a fish for so long I’ve forgotten how they look. I’ve seen a few rabbits over here. Only game I’ve seen.
Well, must close and get supper. All of you write often.
Am feeling great. Hope you are all well.
Love,
Martin
Pvt. M.W. Chandler
Co “C” 117th F.B.S.C.
A.E.F.

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: France on April 4

France 4th
Dearest papa, mama, and all
Have had no chance to write for some time. Received 1 letter from papa and one from Grace and Lorin about 10 days ago. Was surely glad to get them and to know you are all well. They were both dated 2/5. Twas first and only mail I’ve received since being over here. Haven’t received the package tobacco papa sent. It will come in mighty handy cause I haven’t been paid for about 6 months and they haven’t yet received my service record so don’t know when I’ll get paid except will get my service record this month, however.
Are you getting the allotment regularly and did the government add anything? Well I passed a rather different Easter than I generally do. Will certainly remember next Easter where I passed this one. Can’t tell you half that I’d like to. Do you hear often from Ruby and Sam? I wrote them some time ago. Will write Grace, Lorin, and Lucerne tonight – Grace promises me Audrey’s picture for the asking and I sure want it. Seems that I’ve been away from home for ages. I will be 3 years next Dec. 12th. Have lots of real interesting work to do over here. Time just flies. We’re having warm weather. A little rainy but think it will clean up soon. Suppose school is just about ended there for this term isn’t it? How’s Knox getting along? Suppose everything is very high there. Do you have much trouble getting coal and wood?
5 of us have been drawing rations and doing out own cooking past few days account being located quite a distance from the kitchen. Like it fine and dandy. Suppose you read each day of the doings on the Semme and know how things are going. We get the paris edition of the New York Herald here. I don’t have much luck getting news out of a French paper. I can’t speak much French. It’s a hard language to learn.
Well must close for this time. Will write as often as can. Hope this finds you all well.
Lovingly,
Martin
If you send any tobacco select “Bull Durham.” Don’t hand any letters to the paper.

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: France on March 10

France Mar 10th
Dearest Folks,
Will write just few lines tonight while have good chance. Nothing new to write. Have received no mail yet. Suppose it will be several months before you can get a letter to me at this address. Requires quite a while to get an answer to a letter.
Have moved since last writing. Would like to tell you of our locations. Things are pretty warm here.
Been having some very nice weather here for past week. Hope it continues.
I’ve been feeling very good. Get plenty to eat. Have a pretty good YMCA here. Affords a good place to write letters.
Well must close and turn in. Am on K.P. now and have to get up at 4 am.
Hope you are all feeling well.
Will write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin
P.S. Dont have any of my letters put in “Tribune.”

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: France on February 28

Dearest Folks,
Have been traveling about quite a bit since last writing you. Was transferred to the 117th F.B.S.C. Feb 12. Like the organization very well and if I had my mail, clothes, etc from the 1st FB would just as soon stay with this organization. My service record is still with my old company. Don’t know when I’ll get a pay. Haven’t received any pay since October. Would like very much to get the mail you’ve already sent to me at 1st FB. But don’t know whether or not it will be forwarded here.
Been having some very rainy weather the past week. Guess this is the rainy season. First I’ve seen since being over here.
Would like to tell you of our whereabouts but of course that’s forbidden.
Am feeling very good. Only hope you are all feeling as well. Must stop for this time. Will write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin
Address: Pvt. Martin W. Chandler
Co ‘C” 117 F.B.D.C.
A.E.F.
Via New York

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Santa Margarita, California

M.W. Chandler
Santa Margarita, Cal
8034 Santa Margarita

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike Co

Dearest Papa, Mama, and All
Received letter from Papa yesterday and sure glad to get it. I’ve been working 2nd trick for last 2 days. 2nd trick man laid off and man they sent to relieve him couldn’t handle 2nd account so much clerical work to do. Don’t think he can handle 3rd either. Agent wired them that he was putting me on 2nd. Gee I have lots of clerical work to do. Have at least 10 car loads of wood, ore, and apples, each day. Ore all goes to Niagara Falls. Costs $750.00 per car to ship it. Have both Ford and Reed abstracts to make out, damage reports, write up freight bulls in cash book, have to make out Western Union and Tuckit report at end of month. Work from 4 pm to 12 but generally come to work at noon. Came over at noon today and made out ticket report and Western Union up to date. So wouldn’t have so much to do tomorrow. I’ll be on this job for about a week longer and when regular 2nd tick man comes back agent said he would see that I got the 3rd trick back. He came over to hotel and awakened me and asked if I would work 2nd trick. I like the job OK. Get lots of good sleep now. I have 3 passenger trains to sell tickets for and both locals and 2 regular freight trains on this trick but don’t have to get outside of office. Local conductors unload freight and wheel it in warehouse and seal cars and baggage boy handle the passenger trains and check baggage. All I have to do is make out switch lists and clear them. Have quite a few orders but not as many on 3rd trick. Both locals get along between 10 and 11 pm.
Only thing I don’t like about this job is having to work evenings. I’ve been going up to see a bunch of school teachers every night and have lots of fun. Two of them are Catholic and I get into some awful arguments with them some times. All nice girls though. Always have some candy made or a bunch of fruit. Have a swell Victrola and two of them play the piano.
How’s Knox getting along in school? Is Uncle Jim any better? Hope Aunt Sarah is ok.
Well must stop and get busy. Hope you all write soon. Lucerne I haven’t heard from you for a long while. Guess Hipockets is waiting till he learns to spell before he writes. Ha. Will write again soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: France on January 27

France Jan 27
Dearest Folks,
Intended writing yesterday but out it off until today.
Will leave hospital tomorrow but probably wont join my company for a month. Will go from here to convalescent camp and will be there 2 weeks and then go to base where will remain while longer so guess I wont get any mail for some time yet as all my mail will be with company. I haven’t had any pay for 2 months. Guess wont get any until I join company. I’m dead broke too but guess wont have much use for money for while anyway. I’ll have about 40.00 when

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
Mailed From: Ahrweiler, Germany on January 26

Ahrweiler, Germany
Jan 26
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all
Received letter from Papa day before yesterday dated Jan. 1st and very glad to get it and to know everybody is well. Was very anxious to know that Mama and Anna had recovered from the attack of influenza. Think I mentioned in a previous letter that I had received a bunch of my back mail including letters from Ruby, Grace, and Lorin.
Not very much news to write. Persistent rumors indicate that we will leave next month. Most of the rumors sound very plausible and I’m beginning to put a little faith in them. Certainly would love to get home. I’m still on the same job. Business has been rather heavy last few days. Was notified few days ago that I would attend Liaison School at Coblens but have heard nothing definite about it since so don’t know whether or not I’ll go. Hope so anyway.
The people here are as cordial as ever. They don’t seem to be suffering in the least. All the families I’ve seen so far have had plenty of food. I ate supper with a German family (Place where I room) other night and they had roast pork, something I hadn’t tasted for a year.
Has been pretty cold last few days. Has snowed several times lately but not heavily.
Having quite a bit of entertainment through the Red Cross, K of C and YMCA shoes have been pretty good. The 2nd Canadian Division met the 42nd (Rainbow) Division in an athletic contest short time ago. We won the meet by quite a margin. I attended the boxing bouts. We won 5 out of the 6 matches, scoring two knockouts. Had a very large attendance.
Well must close for this time. Want to write to Grace tonight. Wrote to girls at Wichita several days ago.
Hope this finds you all well. I’m feeling fine and dandy. Write often.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Grace Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Grace Chandler
Mailed From: France on January 22

France Jan 22nd
Dearest Grace and all,
has been some time since I’ve written so thought I’d write few lines this pm while nothing to do.
Had a pleasant voyage across the Atlantic. Was on the water Christmas and New Years.
Am in the Hospital here now with measles. Come in the 15th. Am getting along OK and feel good.
Hows Audrey getting along? My I’d love to see her as well as rest of you. It hasn’t been very cold here past 10 days, but has rained considerably.
I expect to join my company in about a week.
Well I can’t say very much so will close. Be sure and write soon as you can. Hope you are all feeling well.
Lovingly,
Martin
Address:
Pvt. M.W. Chandler
Co “B” 1st Fed Bn St. Corpo.
American Evped. Forces
Via New York

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Little Silver, New Jersey

Mr. E. H. Chandler
Pearl, Ill
Pike Co

5th
Dearest papa mama, and all
Received 2 letters from papa day before yesterday. Awful glad to get them. Was just starting home from club and thought would drop you couple lines right quick. Nothing new to write. Don’t know when we will leave. Nobody seems to know. May be here until Christmas and again may leave within the week. We’re all prepared to leave immediately. They fixed up the allotment for me today.
You will get 20.00 about 1st of Nov. and each month from then on for 1 year. I wont have 20 myself to send it home now. Seems like it slips through my fingers just as I get it. Hope everybody is well. Am in hurry just now so will stop and write more some other time.
Feeling fine.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Ruby Chandler, To: Manca
item.description:
From: Ruby Chandler, To: Manca

Monday A.M.
Dearest Manca,
I will write just a note at this time and enclose any letters that have come since I wrote last. Bess said she’d write herself today so she can tell you anything I have left out.
Bess came yesterday (Sun.) noon and Papa was at home too so we had a good visit. She looks fine. She brought each of us something new and brought you a new dress which we’ll make and send you. I want you to visit until your pass limit and rest assured that perhaps all things wont go to “rack and ruin.” Anyway we might get some sewing done for you under stress of your necessity especially while visiting and you know how much that knowledge of necessity can cause us to accomplish at times so we’ll try to get another little package to you before long. I’m sure I appreciate and thank Aunt Annie’s kindness in giving you such a fussy dress. That’s just like her. I was talking to several down at the soldier’s banquet about Uncle’s death and they all had praises for Aunt Annie. Clem Hanback talked as if she Aunt had been her bosom friend.
I’ll send you the papers, too. Martin sent his card here for registration as you’ll see by his letter. Papa had the garden in perfect condition also the lawn and has poled the beans, latticed the tomato plants and planted radishes. Annie has been all I could wish for the past several days. Love to all.
Lovingly,
Ruby

item.title: From: David Knox, To: Annie
item.description:
From: David Kno, To: Annie

To Annie

Dear Annie,
It’s true I have not been writing to you much, since Nettie went up there knowing that you had a chance to hear from some of us pretty often. Would say we were sorry to hear of you being somewhat under the weather but hope ere this you are all right. Bad colds are very common now everywhere. The weather being so changeable no doubt is the cause. Your Ma and I have both had colds and Johnie had a fearful cough at night especially. He is now working everyday now on the section with Honan. Seems to like it very well of course. Mr. Honan is a good friend of his which is some difference. Boys must not have sister do too much and he is all the boys. You tell him I am having this boy in training. He says he know he can output him because he don’t fall down. We are not getting impatient but ply want to see you a lll. Still more so as the expected time draweth near, I see no reason why George cannot come. It is only awhile spent and we all have to submit to losing time if any of us get sick. Try to get him to come. I like the tone of your last letter. It sounds as though you are coming some time , as I said, no use in waiting to get ready. Maggie is now making the machine work and has been for some days, so she will be in practice and have the machine in good order. Maggie is a machinist . She has just finished a dress for her Ma, Lizzie, and herself by some help from Lizzie F. Se says she will teach you all some new styles after you get here. I I suppose the children will be almost as big as she is, as she does not grow a bit. Still she is real handy to do anything she undertakes to do. I have not had a letter from Willie for some 10 days or more. Suppose he is well. He spoke of having bad colds-this is now a fair day. This after noon, but oh how muddy was the slush and snow. Nettie say you have got very big. That will be some surprise to us to see how having got so fresh. Iowa soil must be healthy for you folks as Nettie looks much fresher than when she left. I mean in her posture. Willie talked some of going west. Do you know anything about it? He merely mentioned that he had some notion to do so, but did not say when or positive about it. I will now close as the evening meal is about here and want to send this out. Respects to you all. Hoping to see you all soon in good health and in good spirits. I am as ever your Pa-
David Knox

item.title: From: Jesse, To: Margaret
item.description:
From: Jesse, To: Margaret

Fri Eve 5:40 P.M.
At Home

Dearest One,
As I feel so lonely this P.M. thought I would write you as I haven’t seen you for two or three evenings. That is to converse with you. Sorry it was so that we could not be together last eve. Trusting it will so be I could see you at Sunday School next Lord’s day if not before, trust it will be before. Was up past the house last PM. But could not see you – yourself and your sister’s family’s my sincere heartfelt sympathy in your and their trouble. Trusting the little one will continue to get better. Sorry dear you thought I was mad the eve we were conversing at a distance I sure was not and Margaret I am more than willing to say please a thousand times for you and also do anything I can for to please you.Dearest I will be up by the house at 8 o’clock P.M. and if you can see me a moment would be a pleasure to me. But if not will wait til it is convenient. Trusting you will not think I have advanced a step that I had ought not to of done by writing this.
But dear when I do not get to see you regularly I am lost – I don’t know what I will do when you go to the city.
Margaret – take good care of yourself and do not get sick – as I know you are worn out for you was up all night you must retire early this P.M. and get your regular rest.
Will Close
By By
From your own Boy Jesse

item.title: From: Betty and Harold, To: Millie
item.description:
From: Betty and Harold, To: Millie

Monday
Dearest Aunt Millie,
Again I say I am sorry because I have waited so long to write. About August 10th I took Meiser to Colorado in order to avoid hay fever season in Kans. In less than a week after that I received a long distance phone call from Harold’s doctor in Hearth Platte, Nebraska telling me Harold was seriously ill in hospital with pneumonia. Louie’s wife went to Colorado to care for mother and I left Colo. for He. Platte and joined Harold. He was well enough to leave He. Platte in about three weeks. So we left and we came to Kansas City to see this Dr. Jere who operated on Harold five years ago. We were mistaken about Harold being able to make the trip to Kansas City so back to hospital we went again where he remained another two weeks. He is conversating now and Wed. of this week we go to Topeka for three weeks more of rest. Meier is being brought to Topeka today from Colorado. I am well considering every thing I have seen thru this summer.
I do hope dear you are comfortable and that hay fever did not get you down this summer. Also hope your little dog is well and still with you as I know he is company for you.
Bertie is busy as ever. Louie returned from Europe early last spring and will make no more trips abroad til peace is definitely declared over there which I fear is a long ways off.
Weather here now is beautiful but we had a very hot summer as Ks. always does have.
Hope to hear from you soon and that the report of you health will be favorable.
Lots of love from both of us.
Betty & Harold

item.title: From: Hattie, To: Mill
item.description:
From: Hattie, To: Mill

Dear Aunt Mill
I know we should written sooner but just seemed like we have been so bust with this work all the time and my niece came here right after you were here. She was at the hospital taken treatment and I was there so much and her husband came every weekend and just seemed like there wasn’t any end to the different thing I had to see. I know you would like our house and when you come back be sure and come out to see us as we like to have you. I have had lots of house cleaning to do. I am about thru now. Have been washing up all the curtains. I ironed all day yesterday and not thru yet. Sorry that I hadn’t let you know I had received the scarf and like it very much and I will inclose a dollar in the letter. Hope you are well and enjoying good health.
Heaps of Love
Write Soon
Hattie

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Unknown
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Unknown
Mailed From: Unknown

Business not very heavy just now. Don’t have very many freight trains. It’s getting pretty cold here. Have heavy frosts every night but during day it warms up so don’t need a fire. I get the Tribune regularly. Quite a but of surprising news. Didn’t think Geo Bixby would get married. Don’t see how he is going to support a wife.
How did Ralph make out over stopping no 11 other morning? Gee they sure are strict on this road. Keep the merit and demerit system up all the time. Its called the brown record of discipline. When you get 90 demerits they let you go and no excuses go. I’ve got 10 for dating a train order 8th month in August instead of writing “August” out in full. Guess I’ve got them worked off by now though. They make a fellow toe the mark all around. They’ve eternally got spotters and assistants out on the line watching for every little thing. You can’t connect two words together in a train order not dt an “I” with a circle and all the words must be even distance apart. 2nd trick man here got 10 brownies account two words were too close together in a 19. They bring an order around some time and see if you have it on your file and if they don’t find it they want tot know why you haven’t filed copy of that order. Also send a man over road every month to examine all the operators on books of rules and time card. All the fellows say if you can work for the Southern Pacific you can work for any road in the country. It’s not hard work though, or at least it isn’t here. Don’t have any block wires to contend with. If you haven’t got anything for a train just give them the board. Don’t ever give the rans here the board though cause we’ve got a standing slow order for trains in both directions.
Well guess I’ll stop and get busy. Got quite a few expense bills tonight. Hows Knox coming? Hope to hear from you all soon.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Pike County Republican, To: Martin Chandler
item.description:
From: Pike County Republican, To: Martin Chandler

Mr. Chandler,
I am sorry indeed we are unable to send you the number of papers you asked for. But we ran short last week. Had trouble with the press, and we haven’t found the usual files. But I am sharing two with you and glad to do this.

item.title: From: Martin Chandler, To: Unknown
item.description:
From: Martin Chandler, To: Unknown

Missing Page 1

Page 2:
her today. That’s right Knox. You save all your letters-Ha.
You all needn’t worry about the Mexicans hurting me. I’ve got a Negro gang here and have had ever since I took this camp. Besides all the Mexicans around here are all docile as a lamb. Sure is warm around here. I was in Denison today to do some shopping. Going in again day after tomorrow. Sure hope I get some more mail. Also go in Thursday, so can hold up some niggers checks. They ran off owing me $4.75 in commissary and I want to get it back if I can. The $4.75 will be taken out of my check for next half. I aint get a lick of sense. Think I’ll get most of it back though. Saw in today’s paper where U.S. was going to buy northern Mexico at cost of $300,000,000.
Hope they do – There would probably be a lot of work going on, building railroads, etc. I’m going to stay until end of May so can get few clothes. I’m plume out of style with the duds I’ve got. I’ll get $5.00 day after tomorrow.
Golly it’s sure hot. How’s Aunt Sarah and Uncle Jim? If I stay here until May I’ll be getting at least $35.00.
That letter from Corbett was all right in a way.
He said if I referred to them they would give same information as service letter would carry but didn’t say what kind of information a service letter would carry. That letter was from Herschberger anyway but I’m pretty sure it’s OK and will serve OK. when I look for job telegraphing.
Gee Ralph will need his job telegraphing now wont he?
Golly I weigh 140 pounds and never felt better in my life. Wish it wasn’t so warm. I’ve been taking 5 mile walk to Bona and back nearly every night.
By Golly if the children don’t write pretty soon I’ll not address another letter to them. Knox do you hear that? Now if you want to save up some letters you had better get busy and write.
Is Lucerne going to school in Morrisonville. Gee old Parish sure praises Dr. Thurmon in his paper each week doesn’t he?
Gee I’ll bet Papa sure is busy now. Wish I was there to take few 31st. If I ever go through Kansas City I’m going get that service letter.
Well guess I’d better close. 8:00 pm now and I want to cool off. All write.
Lovingly,
Martin

item.title: From: Ethyl Ransom, To: Ruby Chandler
item.description:
From: Ethyl Ransom, To: Ruby Chandler

Dear Ruby,
Am going to write you a few lines only. Just want to tell you that I am feeling dandy though the weather is pretty hot. Have been working hard but am all through with my sewing. The big event comes off on Tuesday. Only two more days from this. Seems funny! I was in Wichita Thursday. Saw Allan Jones and he told me that you left on Monday the 8th. He said you were one of the prettiest girls he knew. What you think of that? Now Ruby you write to me at Oxford for will be there in a few days. Are you coming back in the fall? Did you take the exam? Give my love to Bess and likewise to Martin. I sure do like that brother of yours. I am sorry I did not meet Grace but I may some time. Did you know Miss M went to Colorado to school? Write soon.
Lovingly,
Ethyl Ransom (yet)

item.title: From: Bess Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family
item.description:
From: Bess Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler and Family

Sunday
Dearest Papa, Mama, and all,
Sure do thank you for then five. Came in handy but I want you to know I earned the money to pay for my Xmas presents. Got $22 for my first case of nursing. No I didn’t either, Mae gave me $10.00 for staying with her. I didn’t want to take that but she just insisted and as I was altogether broke it looked awfully good. Then at Temps I stayed one week and 3 days for $22. Didn’t have anything to do but take care of the little girl. They treated me fine and invited me to stay over Xmas with them and eat turkey dinner but I wanted to eat with the girls. When I left the little girl I was nursing gave me an Xmas present. The sweetest little apron with tattling all around the the pieces set together with tatting wasn’t that nice? I have another place now out on College Hill. Three people down and I’ll get $30.00 a week here. I gave M & L $5.00 between them after Xmas. Lucerne is going to get her a pair of shoes. Margaret got hers and I got mine. They are awfully good looking.
Our Xmas we sent home looked kind of slim didn’t it? I just had one day to shop and I had to wait until I made some money to shop with. I was picking out Xmas cards and found one like the one we sent home. I thought it had lots of good thoughts and it also there was a lot of loving thoughts with out gifts. Grace sent me a pair of silk stockings and Mae gave me a pair too. Mrs. D.D. gave each M, L, and I a drop de china handkerchief. They surely treated Ruby and Sam as well as the rest of us lovely- R & S were going to eat Xmas dinner over there and us girls over to Mae’s but we changed plans and we all ate over to Mary’s and such a dinner. We had a regular one – I’ll let Ruby tell you what she got. Ruby was awfully blue because Sam had to go back.
Margaret has the flu and so far as I can hear is getting along fine. I have to hear thru Mae – She sent her thermometer down by Art. Mae said she would have taken care of Margaret rather than to have her down home at 215 E Dewey but she wasn’t strong yet herself. If Ruby and Lucerne need me I’m willing and ready to go but I thought $30.00 isn’t picked up every week.
Do you hear anything from Martin? Bet he;s anxious to get home. Sure was glad to hear you were all better at home. Ruby, M, and L gave me a flowered petticoat and some handkerchiefs. Think I’ve told you everything Old Santa brought me now. I made Art and the boys a plate of homemade candy and have Mae a pair of Manicure scissors. When did the things arrive home? The girls hadn’t done any shopping to speak of and M and I did most of it Xmas Eve day. The day I went home from Temps.
The baby is getting along fine and Ruby looks well.
Hope to hear from you soon
Love,
Bess

item.title: From: Betty Ann Tilley, To: Amelia J. Wiggins
item.description:
From: Betty Ann Tilley, To: Amelia J. Wiggins

Dearest Aunt Millie,
I have been away from home over a month as Harold had his vacation and we spent most of the time at his home in Catarissa Penna. We drove thru and even though it was twelve hundred miles it seemed like no trip at all. Your card was forwarded to me and as always I was glad to hear from you. I had hoped to get an apt. here but we have a vacancy in one of the apts. at some and besides mother is not at all well so tomorrow Harold is taking me to Topeka and at Xmas he will come to be with us. If at all possible I shall return here at that time with him. It is very difficult for me to leave mother at all and we can not always arrange to have her with us as it is not possible for her to have her comforts any place like at “Home Sweet Home.” I do hope darling you are well and have things comfortable. To be in a warm home is a lot to be thankful for, so many poor people suffer in cold weather. Speaking of weather, ever have we had such a fall even now winter has not arrived and its nearing Xmas. My little dog is sitting on the window sill looking down on the street, guess she thinks she is directing traffic as she growls when ever a dog passes or anything else she doesn’t like the looks of. Aunt Millie have you tried during the past few years to get glasses? Maybe you need new ones. It’s a shame for you not to have them if you could see better.
Poor mother nothing helps her any, neither the operation nor glasses and it make me very sad. She still sees enough to get around the house and neighborhood but that is about all. I miss her and her interesting letters. I am trying to write larger so you can read my letter more easily. Do you ever hear from Lela? After all the money you spent on the child its pitiful that she isn’t with you when you do need her so badly. I wish it was so I could see you at least occasionally but I can scarcely leave mother to even be with my very good husband.
I received a letter from Bertie yesterday. He keeps well but so busy he hardly has time to go see mother. His two younger daughters are away to school. One in Chicago and the other in Lawrence, Ks. He sees them both often as he has to make frequent trips to Chicago.
I shall close now dearest Auntie and take my little dog out for a stroll. Again I shall say that I hope my letter finds you well and happy. Am glad you have so many good friends.
Love and a kiss,
Your devoted niece,
Betty Ann Tilley
Enclosed are a few stamps for your convenience.

item.title: From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
item.description:
From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
Mailed From: Albuquerque, New Mexico on March 6, 1892

European Hotel.
Corner First Street and Railroad Avenue.
Frank E. Sturges, Proprietor.
Albuquerque, N.M. Mch 6th, 1892
My Dear Wife
I will write you this morning. This is the first chance I have had to write any. I got here in the after part of last night. Am well and I trust this will find all of you well. I am awful anxious to hear from you but I can not say yet whether I will get to go to Prescalt or not. This being Sunday I have no chance to see any one so I can find out whether they will grant me a pass or not. This is a nice city and the people are very sociable. I am tired from riding on the cars. Did not get to sleep very much until this morning went to bed about three o’clock and sleep till eight. I saw some nice country coming down here and some very rough. It rained from the time I left K City Friday morning until some time in the night and then commenced S. morning and snowed until yesterday evening. There is some snow on the ground here and the mountains are wet with snow. The snow was 14 inches deep in Colorado and I thought some time the train would stop they went so slow. I can’t hardly describe how it looked going up the mountains. The train had two heavy engines and they did not go as fast as a man could walk. I will not try to give any further description of the country but will tell you when I come home. If I don’t get passed over the A & P I will not go to Prescalt. If I do get them I will telegraph to you so you can write to me. Everything here is high and I can’t afford to fool away money trying to dead head my way with train men. I would give any thing if I was with you and the children now. Kiss the children for me. Tell Vinnie I think of her too. I have written to you each morning since I left. I hope you are enjoying your self. I will close and write to you again tomorrow but not until often I find out what I am going to do. I will have to stay here tonight I guess.
Good bye,
From your Loving Husband,
E.H. Chandler

item.title: From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
item.description:
From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
Mailed From: Pearl, Illinois on July 24, 1887

Miss Nettie Knox
Sidney, Ia.
Freemaut Co

Pearl, July 24, ’87
Dear Nettie
Your kind letter of 21st. Just saw and read with great pleasure. I will try to answer this eve. I was in hopes the next letter I got from you I would hear you was going to be for home right away. Well two weeks want be very long to want because I am very anxious to see you. I went to the festival the other night and had a very good time but didn’t have any pictures. I am just about sick today and have been for two or three days. I was up till about one o’clock the night of the festival. Then Winslaw woke me at 2:30 to work for him. He came to St. Louis. So I had to work that day and till 12:15 the next night. So I guess that is what the matter with me. The men have had a bad time this pat day. It was raining and many of them were at work. So, the most of them got stuck or usual. This is a fine day and all the men are at work and I am glad of it. I get disgusted with lots of old drunken men. Well, I do wish you had come home in time to have taken sleigh ride. maybe it will snow again before winter’s close. If it doesn’t I expect it will snow next winter but I don’t like to wait so I’ll leave it at that. I am at a loss to know what to write today, nothing worth writing about. Oh, certainly I will excuse you for not answering that letter as you was busy and fixing to come home. But not for anything else. Well I guess I will have to close for want of something to write. But never mind I will pay up when you come home. Yes be sure to let me know when you are coming. I would be happy to come meet you. Hoping to heat from you again soon.
I am Yours Truly,
E.H. Chandler

item.title: From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
item.description:
From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler

Miss Nettie Knox
Sidney, Ia.
Freenaut Co.

Pearl, January 6th ’87
Dear Nettie,
I just received your kind letter of January 1st and was glad to hear from you. I have been looking for a letter for three or four days. I am sorry your face and hands both broke out like you told me but I hope you will be all right soon. I read one of your letter you wrote to Maggie some time ago about your face being broke out but you did not say anything to me about it before. There is nothing new to write. Good snow on the ground and has been awful cold for the last week. Maggie and Lizzie went sleigh riding today. They went up to Lizzie’s mother. They just got back at 6 pm. No I haven’t been sleigh riding yet this winter. One reason I have not went was because I did not have a sleigh and don’t have such time to look after one. But I expect if you was here I could find time and a sleigh too. Willie is here yet. He lost his pocket book the other day with about 30 dollars in it. That’s what I call bad luck. I got a litter from Soruby today. He wanted me to write him a letter of recommend. I did not have time today, will tomorrow. One of the Broker men on the way freight going East this a.m. got both legs cut off. I did not see him as it happened at Roadhouse. Frank Ward was down the other day but he didn’t call in to see Lizzie. I guess William has got him done up. Mrs. Laux has moved back to the Cattoye Hatil again, Siul’s had their dance new year’s eve and had a big drunken fight. We had a show in town today. A man and a bear. The man was leading the bear and about 5 hundred kids after him more or less. No Anthany has not been here for some time. Maynard has gone to Nebraska. They have not done anything about the church house yet. The people of Old Pearl would give up the house out there. There is a petition here in town asking to the trustees to donate 5 hundred dollars of the town money to build a Christian church. The most of the people have signed it. I can’t say how it will be fixed. I haven’t heard from Phillips since I wrote to you. Only I asked the man where he had gone. He said P. was working at Waun on the I and 5th. Oh no, I don’t think you could do anything with me if you was here. I just make the girls fly around. I expect I would do you the same way if you was here. Well, the girls could get away with me now if they knew I was crippled. I fell down on the platform yesterday and hit by back on a plank. It’s pretty sore but I did not tell any of them so they think I am OK. I don’t want you to tell Maggie about it. If I had been there new year I bet I could have fixed your hair for you but I guess you have combed it before now. Well I have written all I can think of this p.m. Give my regards to all. And my love to you.
Your’s Truly,
E.H. Chandler

item.title: From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
item.description:
From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
Mailed: February 4, 1887 from R.P.O

Miss Jeanette Knox
Sidney, Ia.
Heewaut Co.

Pearl Feb. 4th ’87
Dear Nettie
Your warm, kind letter of love, just received and read with great pleasure. Will now try and answer too. Has been a long time since I heard from you but I hope to see you soon then that will pay for waiting. Mrs. Attwell died last night, funeral service tomorrow at the church house. They have sent for Brother Authey to lead the funeral and have not got any answer yet. I don’t know whether he will agree or not. I got a letter from Mr. Weedles today. He said if I thought Jae could do the work I might send him to Sinclair next Tuesday morning. Now I am going to let him try it. If he works a failure I can’t help it. Sinclair is a small place and not hardly any thing to do so if he can’t get along there he can’t anywhere else. Yes Jae and Will Maymard are going with the Well’s girls and I think they are both pretty boldly gave. I am all right today. I had the tooth taken out before I received your advice about it. I went to Sailor’s Lament last night at the church house. it was very good. Yes I think you had better write when you will reach Whitehall as a letter might be delayed. The Crusher is not working this week they have a breakdown. There will be a good change for a sleigh ride yet this winter. Although there aint any snow on the ground here but it looks like snowing. Now I have told you all. I love to write to you but hope I won’t have to write any other time. Write please, see you soon.
Yours truly,
E.H. Chandler

item.title: From: Jeanette Knox Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Jeanette Knox Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Sidney, Iowa on February 1st ’87

Sidney, Iowa Feb 1st ’87
Mr. E.H. Chandler
My Dearest Friend,
Your most welcome letter received last eve and perused with the greatest of pleasure and now I will try to write a few lines in answer. It seems if you have the same kind of weather there as we have here, I will get to take a sleigh ride with you sure enough if it does not turn warm and thaw the snow off before I get there. It is snowing very fast this am and there is a good deal of snow already on the ground. There is no fear of my changing my mind about coming home for I am only to anxious to get started. I expect I had better wire you what time I will start. Annie think stat would be best. I am truly sorry to hear of you suffering so much with your tooth. Annie say’s for me to tell you that she said for you to have that tooth taken out immediately. So I guess you had better do so. I have not received my money from home yet as Maggie said she would send it in next letter. I expect it today or tomorrow. Then after that gets here there is no telling what time I will rack out for home but I should say, rather shortly. I have felt sorry many times because I did not answer that letter of yours because since then, instead of getting two letters from you, I only get one in the same length of time and it seems such along time to wait for one letter comes until I get another from you, but Oh! how nice to think, we will soon see each other and then can talk instead of writing. Not that I tire of writing oh no – I have always found that a pleasure. But it will give me more pleasure still, to see and talk to you. I suppose the fox chase was quite an exciting affair for the people of Peal and other towns. But I fear the next report I hear of it will be that the crowd all stayed at Pearl the most of the night and got drunk and had a general tear up. That is what I expect to hear in next report. Yes – if Johnie had sen there he would also have been in the five and I think Nettie would have been too, if she had been there. Does Joe try to go with anybody? When I was at home the girls (Lizzie and Maggie) said he had been going some with May Hess. But I never seen them together while I was there. That is too bad that Matt Mulligan was so unfortunate as to loose his position as night watch by that explosion. I suppose he can not get a job at the grocery store any more at all. Well I am surprised to hear of Sell Strunk’s break, as I was in hopes Sell would change his ways after George’s death and after his joining the church but it seems he has failed. Well now I will close. John has just returned from the office and I did not get a letter from Maggie. Write soon.
Yours Lovingly,
Nettie

item.title: From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
item.description:
From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
Mailed From: Pearl, Illinois on January 12, 1887

item.title: From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
item.description:
From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
Mailed From: Pearl, Illinois on January 19, 1887

Miss Nettie Knox
Sidney, Ia
Freemont Co

Pearl, Ill Jan 19, 1887
Dear Nettie,
I just received your kind letter of 16th will try and answer this pm. I was glad to hear from you and to hear you have concluded to come home. Well if you can let me know what day you will start for home. If you come by the way of White Hall let me know what day you will be there and I will meet you in Whitehall and if you should take a notion to come soon other way let me know. I was surprised when Maggie told me the other day that you was coming home. You can imagine about how glad I was but I can’t tell you. When you get this letter and are going to start soon. Answer about 2 days before you leave and be sure and say what day you expect to reach Whitehall. Now will not write but a short letter this time but hope to see you soon then I can tell you all. I am busy today. Mae is sick. I guess he has not been at the depot today. Oh, yes we had quite an explosion at the quarry last night or this morning, the powder house exploded. No one hurt as there was no one there but Matt Mulligan and he happened to be out of the way. There was 7 hundred pound went off. It made a big rocket. It woke me up. So you may know it had to be pretty loud. Now will close hoping to hear from you soon.
I am yours truly,
E.H. Chandler

item.title: From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
item.description:
From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
Mailed From: Pearl, Illinois on January 15, 1887

Miss Nettie Knox
Sidney, Ia.
Freemaut Co.

Pearl, Ill Jan 15th ’87
Dear Nettie,
I received your kind letter yesterday and was glad to hear from you again as I always am. I will try and answer this morning but don’t know how I will make it. Nothing to write about. They are going to have a festival at the church house next Friday night. They had a county meeting last night. Everybody is going to the fox chase today. I was glad to hear you are getting all right again. Yes I suppose the Dr. thought you was a good patient. He gave a visiting when he went to see you. I will be glad when your time is out in Iowa. It seems to me like you have been gone 6 years now. I let Maggie read the letter you wrote in answer to the one I told you about falling down on the platform. She liked to have taking a fit about it. I think the snow will go off and spare the sleighing if it don’t turn cold pretty soon. This morning looks like a spring morning. Well I will be glad when spring comes again. I am getting tired staying in side so much. When does Johny think he will come home? Yes Nettie your letters are all interesting to me whether they are long or short. I don’t think Jae will get a job soon but he could if he was a good operator. Theres a good chance for Operators now on this road. I thought yesterday I would see what Jae would do if he was alone. So I told him when the conductor signed the order to get it corrected. I was out in the passenger room. Jae gave the conductor signature to the order. Then the dispatcher asked him if the train was all ready to go. Jae near made him any answer then asked him again and Jae asked him what he said. Then the dispatcher said where is E. By that time I went in and fixed them up. It seems to me that Jae don’t try to learn anything. I have gave him a good chance but I am not going to recumbent him until I know he can do what they want him to do. Jae has made a move on all of the Wells girls. Him and Billy Maynard both go out to Wells. Now they are awful thick. Now I will close for this time. Hopeful to hear from you soon. With all my love to you.
I am yours Truly,
E.H. Chandler

item.title: From: Jeanette Knox Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Jeanette Knox Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Sidney, Iowa on January 12, 1887

Mr. E.H. Chandler
Dear Lize,
Your most welcome letter received and contents perused with pleasure. I suppose you will not find this letter very interesting and am at a lose to know or think of anything to write at a lll. So if you find it very dry, please excuse for this time and perhaps I can do better next time. I have been doing lots of running around the past two or three days. Last Monday I spent the day with Miss Mary Hicks and yesterday I was working on fancy work all day at the milliner shop and today will go again. So you see I am making up for when I had to stay at home. Monday while I was at Miss Hick’s the Dr. came up to see how I was getting along and low and behold I was visiting. I guess he thought I was a rather pert patient. Don’t you think so too? yes, I guess Willie is pretty tired of Pearl by this time but Pa said in one of his letters to me that he was going to try to get Willie to stay the balance of the winter there at home. But I fear he will not succeed for I think Willie would nearly die to stay there and have nothing to do. That was too bad about that poor man that had his legs cut off and I think it was a good thing that death did claim him as he always would have been such a bad cripple. Do you know what his name is? This is a lovely day and so pleasant. There is a splendid sleighing snow on the ground and the sleigh just more than fly. Where does Scrooge work about? I suppose Joe thinks he is competent to be Opr. Agent and all in one. Will he get a job and if so, where? I think the different R.R. Co’s were very good to remember you so kindly by sending you such presents as you named in you letter. Well I would like to have seen Lizzie and Maggie when their sleigh broke down. I know I would have laughed. Has Pa got a sleigh or who’s do they use. Well I must now close and go up town to my work. Good-bye with my love to you.
I am ever yours,
Nettie
(I would like to talk to you 2 or 3 days_
Write Soon.

item.title: From: Jeanette Knox Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
item.description:
From: Jeanette Knox Chandler, To: Elijah H. Chandler
Mailed From: Sidney, Iowa on January 9, 1887

Sidney, Iowa, jan. 9th, 18887
Sunday Eve.
Mr. E. H. Chandler
Dear Lige,
Your most welcome letter received yesterday and contents read with pleasure as it had been a long time it seemed to me since I had heard from you.
It took my letter of the 1st longer time to reach you than usual. I wrote you another before that one dated December 29th I believe. It surely did not reach you as you said you had been looking for a letter from me for 2 or 3 days. and I did not get any answer to it. I need your telegram today about 1/2 past 3 o’clock. I am sorry you were so uneasy about me but I appreciate your kindness to me more than I can express. I did not answer your telegram as I am sure Maggie received a letter from me today and it will say how I am and knowing they would let you know I thought it no use to answer the telegram as the letter will be there sooner than it anyway. I am now about all right with the exception of a very severe cold. My eyes are now all right except a little weak yet. My face is clear of the breaking – out, but there is some signs of it still on my hands. I have not been, to say, sick at all only while my eyes were so very sore I kept to my bed most of 2 or 3 days. I have not been out of doors this past week but I expect to go up town tomorrow if the day is not stormy. I was so frightened when the Express Agent brought me the telegram today I could scarcely open it. I thought so of you were very sick and perhaps it was calling me home. Oh! how glad I would be to be there. I would give anything to see you but now it is a little over 2 months to wait until that time comes. I am so glad to have your picture when I get to thinking of you I can get your pictures and look at it, if I can’t see you personally. I look at it 5 or 6 times a day. I see you still have that pin with “N” on it. It looms up in the picture. Every time I show it to anyone here they notice the pin and ask me if it is mine. I tell them it used to be. Johnnie and some more of the town boys have been sawing ice. They are not done yet. I tell you we have to get up a little earlier while he is at work. But today being Sunday we did not have to get up so early. While we were at our breakfast, Johnnie said we were eating our dinner and I asked him why he said that. He said it was just twelve o’clock (noon) and I did not believe it and left the table to look at the clock, and sure enough it was 12-5. Wasn’t we early? Do you ever get up so early?
Oh! Oh! Mister! You think you would treat me the same as the other girls if I was there. Do you? Well now I guess you wouldn’t, I have something to say about that. I could not help but laugh when I read in your letter about you falling on the platform. It would have been a picnic for Lizzie and Maggie if they had seen you about that time. I am sorry to hear of Willie’s misfortune but I had heard of it before. I suppose he will never find his pocket book not hear anything of it again. Oh! Yes – I suppose Frank Williams has Frank Woods done up. It would not surprise me very much if William and Lizzie marry. Pa said in one of his letters that they was afraid Williams would cause them to offer up another girl before the winter is over.
What do you think about it? Say tell Lizzie J. For me that I am just as Mad as I can be at her because she has not answered my letter.
I would like to have seen the show you told me about (The Man and Bear) I think I should have enjoyed it ever so much. Oh! I do hope they will succeed in getting the money to build the church with. That would be so nice. I can hardly write as I am using my knee for a writing desk. You will please excuse writing and lead pencil. Now I will close as it is bedtime. Oh! I forgot to tell you that I got my hair combed New Year’s day but I expect if you have been here you could have did a better job of it. I did not style up one but today if it is true. I am getting old fast but I am yours,
Nettie

item.title: From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
item.description:
From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
Mailed From: Pearl, Illinois on December 29, 1886

Miss Nettie Knox
Sidney, Ia.
Freemaut Co.

Pearl, Dec 29th ’86
Dear Nettie,
Your kind letter of 25th received today. I was surely glad to hear from you. Oh yes I got the cup yesterday. Everything in good order I think it is awfully nice and is a very suitable gift. I haven’t used it now yet. Maggie was awful anxious to see what was in the box for her. I opened it then went over to the house to tease Maggie. I told her I got the cup but there was nothing for her.
Willie K arrived last night from St. Louis. He thinks he will remain in Pearl awhile. There is king to be a concert Friday night at the church house. Oh yes I got a Christmas card from Miss N. of Jacksonville but I knew it by the handwrite on envelope. There is a good snow on the ground. If you were here I would like to go sleigh riding. I haven’t had a ride this winter. Willie was asking me about Miss Emma. I expect he will be out sleigh riding pretty soon. I think they are going to have a big time at Duke’s Saturday night.
I am having a good time this week not much work to do, but I expect to pay for it after the holidays are over. I guess you have a good time buying Christmas presents for the children. We’ll I hope you may have a good time new year, there aint nothing going on in Pearl today and nothing to write about. I believe you can beat me writing good long letters. Well I will have to close for this time. Hoping to hear from you soon.
I am your truly,
E.H. Chandler
P.S. I heard from Phillips today. Jr was talking to him on the well. He is working nights at Edwardsville junction for another road.
Lovingly Yours,
E.

item.title: From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler
item.description:
From: Elijah H. Chandler, To: Jeanette Knox Chandler

Miss Nettie Knox
Sidney, Ia
Freenaut Co.

Pearl, December 29th, ’86
Dear Nettie,
Your ind letter of 20th received today. I was sure glad to hear from you. Oh yes I got the cup yesterday. Everything in good order. I think it is awful nice and is a very suitable gift. I haven’t used it now yet. Maggie was awful anxious to see what was in the box for her. I opened it there, went over to the house to tease Maggie. I told her I got the cup but there was nothing for her. Willie K. arrived last night from St. Louis.
